{"arxiv_id":"2611.09777","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Mon, 09 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.09777"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":80,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2611.09777v1 Announce Type: new \nAbstract: Snake robots can leverage their hyper-redundant morphology for both locomotion and manipulation through distributed body contact but whole-body loco-manipulation is particularly challenging since the entire body serves simultaneously as propulsive mechanism and manipulation tool Prior work on wheeled legged and snake robot platforms has decoupled these functions through dedicated appendages body segmentation or grippers We present closed-loop loco-manipulation with our snake robot COBRA without this distinction such that any part of the body may make contact We develop a contact-implicit dynamic model unifying robot-ground robot-object and object-ground interactions within a Moreau-Jean time-stepping framework and formulate a trajectory optimization over the full-order dynamics guided by a geometric planner and nominal proportional controller to autonomously push an object to a goal location during sidewinding We validate the planner and controller on hardware across varied configurations and present simulation results for a simplified trajectory optimization that resolves robot-object and object-ground contacts","title":"Autonomous Whole-body Loco-manipulation Using a Snake Robot","title_en":"Autonomous Whole-body Loco-manipulation Using a Snake Robot","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.09777","version":null,"version_updated_at":null}

{"arxiv_id":"2611.12870","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Tue, 10 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.12870"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":50,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2611.12870v1 Announce Type: cross \nAbstract: World action models jointly predict video and actions conditioned on language. Existing studies focus primarily on architectures and training mechanisms, typically treating language-video alignment acquired through video pretraining as an established foundation. However, introducing action learning may impair this alignment. Principled guidance on data and supervision design for maintaining language-video alignment during action learning remains limited. To investigate this, we curate a pool of approximately 47,000 hours of general videos, egocentric videos, UMI demonstrations, and robot demonstrations. Building on this, we systematically study how language-video supervision, language-video-action supervision, and the joint use of these two forms affect WAM performance. In particular, we examine how language annotation quality affects pretrained language-video capabilities, and how action supervision from UMI and robot demonstrations extends these capabilities to language-video-action modeling. To better scale the model, we further conduct detailed studies on joint training recipe and model architecture. Under a fixed training budget, mixing egocentric videos and UMI demonstrations improves control generalization. Model architecture affects how effectively these experiences are used, while scaling pretraining under the selected configuration brings further gains. The resulting recipe, post-trained on RoboTwin Clean demonstrations only, achieves success rates of 88.10% and 61.56% under Easy (Clean-to-Clean) and Hard (Clean-to-Random) conditions, respectively. Our model achieves 40.00% SR across three real-world tasks, compared with 23.33% for the strongest baseline, indicating better generalization under unseen conditions. We release the curated data, training code, and model weights.","title":"SWAM: Scaling World Action Models with Cross-Modal Alignment","title_en":"SWAM: Scaling World Action Models with Cross-Modal Alignment","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12870","version":null,"version_updated_at":null}

{"arxiv_id":"2611.12767","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Tue, 10 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.12767"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":50,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2611.12767v1 Announce Type: cross \nAbstract: Autonomous vehicles track planned trajectories close to obstacles. Unknown disturbances make them deviate from these trajectories. With a bound on the tracking error that disturbances can cause, a planned trajectory can be certified as safe before execution. Existing set-based methods bound the tracking error by one invariant ellipsoid for the whole trajectory or by intervals, which are both conservative. For aerial and space vehicles, the tracking error evolves on a matrix Lie group with nonlinear dynamics. However, for group-affine systems, the error dynamics are linear in Lie algebra coordinates when the vehicle receives the inputs of the reference. The control input and the disturbance enter through the inverse right Jacobian, a matrix that depends on the error. We propagate the linear part of the error dynamics with zonotopes and enclose the effect of the inverse right Jacobian on the disturbance in closed form. The resulting tubes are tight and provably contain all reachable tracking errors in continuous time. When some error components have no input, the inverse right Jacobian leaves unmatched nonlinear terms in the closed loop. None of the tested methods certifies such a closed loop. Hybrid coordinates make these terms matched, so that our controller cancels every nonlinear term that does not contain the disturbance. Our tubes give tighter bounds than the ellipsoid method in simulations of a planar aircraft and a fully actuated multirotor and in real flights of a quadrotor, where the tube contains every measured attitude error. Under larger disturbances and the same feedback gain, the ellipsoid method yields no valid ellipsoid, whereas our tubes remain valid.","title":"Certified Zonotopic Reachability Analysis for Trajectory Tracking on Lie Groups","title_en":"Certified Zonotopic Reachability Analysis for Trajectory Tracking on Lie Groups","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12767","version":null,"version_updated_at":null}

Uniformly instantiating detections at different scales as 3D objects can be brittle for small on-surface items; without explicit object-state validation, stale entries may persist after scene changes. Our key insight is to separate persistent 3D furniture entities from revisable surface-object hypotheses, retaining their visual evidence without requiring independent object geometry. We formalize this design as the Hypothesis Scene Graph (HSG), which preserves small-object evidence and supports local revision without rebuilding the stable entity topology. Building on HSG, HSGNav uses this separation for multi-scale lifelong navigation: retrieval selects entity or hypothesis evidence according to target scale, exploration acquires additional surface observations, and verification confirms target presence or invalidates contradicted hypothesis records. Because existing lifelong benchmarks such as GOAT-Bench rarely require mid-episode memory invalidation or multi-scale search, we introduce FAROS-Bench (Find And Re-find Objects across Scales) for mid-episode relocation of surface objects and multi-scale find goals. Experiments show that HSGNav performs competitively on GOAT-Bench while substantially outperforming prior methods on FAROS-Bench.","title":"HSGNav: Hypothesis Scene Graphs for Multi-Scale Lifelong Navigation under Object Relocation","title_en":"HSGNav: Hypothesis Scene Graphs for Multi-Scale Lifelong Navigation under Object Relocation","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.10547","version":null,"version_updated_at":null}

The regime that allows collisions between the moving robot and the operator, called Power and Force Limiting (PFL), restricts the permissible contact forces. Using the same fixed contact thresholds on the entire robot surface results unnecessary productivity losses, as the robot needs to stop even when impact forces are within limits. Here we present a framework that decides whether the robot should interrupt motion based on estimated collision force computed individually for different parts of the robot body and dynamically on the fly, based on the Effective Mass (EM) of each robot link. We performed experiments on a simulated and real collaborative robot arm (UR10e) with sensitive skin (AIRSKIN) for collision detection and isolation. To demonstrate the generality of our method, we added experiments on simulated KUKA LBR iiwa robot, where collision sensing draws on joint torque sensing. On a mock pick-and-place scenario with both transient and quasi-static collisions, we show an increase in productivity over 45% from using the standard approach. The method is applicable to any robot for which the EF can be calculated.","title":"Adaptive Collision Sensitivity for Efficient and Safe Human-Robot Collaboration","title_en":"Adaptive Collision Sensitivity for Efficient and Safe Human-Robot Collaboration","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.20184","version":null,"version_updated_at":null}

{"arxiv_id":"2212.01506","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Tue, 10 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2212.01506"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":50,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2212.01506v3 Announce Type: replace \nAbstract: In this paper, we present a computer vision-based approach to measure the sizes and growth rates of apple fruitlets. Measuring the growth rates of apple fruitlets is important because it allows apple growers to determine when to apply chemical thinners to their crops in order to optimize yield. The current practice of obtaining growth rates involves using calipers to record sizes of fruitlets across multiple days. Due to the number of fruitlets needed to be sized, this method is laborious, time-consuming, and prone to human error. With images collected by a hand-held stereo camera, our system, segments, clusters, and fits ellipses to fruitlets to measure their diameters. The growth rates are then calculated by temporally associating clustered fruitlets across days. We provide quantitative results on data collected in an apple orchard, and demonstrate that our system is able to predict abscise rates within 3.5% of the current method with a 6 times improvement in speed, while requiring significantly less manual effort. Moreover, we provide results on images captured by a robotic system in the field, and discuss the next steps required to make the process fully autonomous.","title":"Autonomous Apple Fruitlet Sizing and Growth Rate Tracking using Computer Vision","title_en":"Autonomous Apple Fruitlet Sizing and Growth Rate Tracking using Computer Vision","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.01506","version":null,"version_updated_at":null}

{"arxiv_id":"2611.11934","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Tue, 10 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.11934"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":70,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2611.11934v1 Announce Type: cross \nAbstract: The wide field of view of fisheye cameras and the simplicity of a monocular setup make monocular fisheye visual odometry (VO) attractive for robotic localization and mapping. Nevertheless, scale drift remains a major challenge over long trajectories. Unsupervised depth learning can help to mitigate this issue, but the pronounced distortion of fisheye images poses challenges for accurate depth estimation. This article presents S$^2$D-FVO, a monocular fisheye VO framework integrating spherical bundle adjustment (SBA)-guided unsupervised depth learning to improve scale consistency and depth estimation accuracy. Given that pixel reprojection residuals do not uniformly reflect angular deviations between viewing rays and that the first-order linearization of a scalar angular reprojection residual is insensitive to perturbations along one tangent direction, SBA employs tangent-space angular reprojection residuals derived from the spherical logarithmic map. These residuals retain sensitivity along both tangent directions, with their norms equal to the corresponding scalar angular residuals. A median depth-based scale regularization term is further integrated into SBA to constrain the reconstruction scale. Building on these formulations, SBA replaces the pose estimation network during unsupervised depth learning, providing more reliable relative poses for view synthesis. In turn, depth estimates from the well-trained depth estimation network provide scale references for SBA, improving scale consistency while allowing individual 3-D landmark positions to be refined. Extensive experiments conducted on multiple public datasets, as well as two newly collected large-scale datasets, demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms representative existing approaches in both depth and trajectory estimation accuracy and is applicable to different camera models.","title":"Scale-Consistent Monocular Fisheye Visual Odometry via Spherical Bundle Adjustment-Guided Unsupervised Depth Learning","title_en":"Scale-Consistent Monocular Fisheye Visual Odometry via Spherical Bundle Adjustment-Guided Unsupervised Depth Learning","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.11934","version":null,"version_updated_at":null}

{"arxiv_id":"2606.04746","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Tue, 10 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2606.04746"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":40,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2606.04746v4 Announce Type: replace \nAbstract: Multi-Agent Path Finding (MAPF) algorithms are increasingly used to plan motion for robot teams in industrial warehouses and robotic shared workspaces, but standard MAPF algorithm evaluation metrics, such as Sum of Costs (SoC), makespan, and planner runtime, can obscure how planner choices translate into realistic execution performance. We present CADENCE (Coordination and Action-Driven Estimation for Networked Continuous Execution), a hardware study of this evaluation gap on a fixed 7 by 7 workcell with seven differential drive robots, asking which features available before execution can best predict final wall-clock completion time. We compare SoC, total planned travel cost, primitive motion burden (how much basic motion the plan requires, such as makespan, turns, consecutive moves, and start-stop transitions), and interaction aware coordination structure (how much inter-robot coordination the plan induces, such as dependency links, interacting robot pairs, dependency depth, and crowding exposure). To test this, we generate 120 plans across 15 scenarios -- 5 Empty, 5 Medium Random, and 5 Bottleneck and execute each plan four times, yielding a 480 trial hardware corpus. Using both a scenario-held -- out ridge model and a trial-level mixed-effects model, we find that SoC alone is informative but incomplete, while primitive motion burden gives the strongest improvement, reducing held out error by about 48.6%-59.8% in MAE and 44.2%-61.4% in RMSE relative to SoC-only models. Interaction-aware coordination features add smaller, less uniform gains, most clearly in the mixed-effects analysis. Across both models and uncertainty checks, primitive motion burden is the most reliable additional signal beyond SoC, suggesting that much of the execution time gap is already visible in the offline plan before any robot starts moving.","title":"CADENCE: Predicting Realized MAPF Execution Time Beyond Sum of Costs","title_en":"CADENCE: Predicting Realized MAPF Execution Time Beyond Sum of Costs","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.04746","version":null,"version_updated_at":null}

This paper revisits rotary drone design by exploring which body morphologies are best suited for different objectives and constraints. An evolutionary algorithm is used to produce drone morphologies that performs better than standard configurations at thrust-to-weight ratio, maneuverability and size. To generate a range of drones with performance trade-offs between them, the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II is used. {"arxiv_id":"2611.10682","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Tue, 10 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.10682"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":70,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2611.10682v1 Announce Type: new \nAbstract: Learning whole-body musculoskeletal control from human motion is important for developing human-like robots, assistive devices, and rehabilitation systems. This task presents two main challenges, namely reference trajectories that are kinematically plausible but difficult to reproduce through muscle-driven dynamics, and a highly redundant 700-dimensional action space in which unstructured exploration can easily disrupt the target motion. In this paper, we propose a motion-to-policy pipeline that exploits muscle redundancy in two complementary stages. First, muscle-aware retargeting (MAR) performs bounded adaptation of kinematic trajectories subject to hard semantic, anatomical, and contact constraints. We motivate the constraint bounds by analyzing how reference-trajectory artifacts affect muscle-driven tracking. Second, null-space exploration (NSE) estimates a one-control-frame mapping from muscle excitations to generalized forces and injects bounded, anatomically structured perturbations along its null space into the actions of a value-guided flow policy. On a 24-clip motion-capture benchmark, MAR and NSE together solve every reference, reach the full horizon with half the samples of the baseline pipeline, and lower joint-center error by 44% without late collapse. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first end-to-end pipeline that transforms monocular video into a trained whole-body imitation policy controlling 700 muscles.","title":"Burden, Bounty, or Bliss? Muscle-Aware Retargeting and Null-Space Exploration for Whole-Body Musculoskeletal Control","title_en":"Burden, Bounty, or Bliss? Muscle-Aware Retargeting and Null-Space Exploration for Whole-Body Musculoskeletal Control","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.10682","version":null,"version_updated_at":null}

{"arxiv_id":"2605.20299","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Mon, 09 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2605.20299"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":50,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2605.20299v2 Announce Type: replace-cross \nAbstract: Generative sequence models are often trained to plan motion in physical domains, from robotics to mechanical simulations. When constructing a dataset to train such a model, engineers may curate demonstrations to specify how trajectories should be distributed over a physical quantity like travel distance or mechanical energy. For example, a roboticist building a maze navigation agent might choose demonstrations whose travel distances cover a fixed range uniformly, hoping to constrain the agent's expected power usage. We find that standard deep learning can violate this intent: each generated trajectory can seem plausible on its own, but the aggregate distribution over the physical quantity is wrong. We call this failure physical misgeneralization. In this work, we identify and formalize the problem, develop and validate an account of its mechanism, and use that account to compare and design mitigations. Using controlled synthetic tasks, we show that physical misgeneralization arises when local errors typical of the model class propagate through the physical measurement to shift the recovered distribution. We estimate these errors with a data deviation kernel, and we use it to predict which physical quantity values gain or lose mass under real diffusion sequence models trained on both toy and applied trajectory generation tasks. Finally, our mechanistic interpretation helps identify which mitigations are structurally promising. We benchmark Diffusion Policy across 12 different tasks from 4 different robot manipulation benchmarks and find that it consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art robot learning methods with an average improvement of 46.9%. Diffusion Policy learns the gradient of the action-distribution score function and iteratively optimizes with respect to this gradient field during inference via a series of stochastic Langevin dynamics steps. We find that the diffusion formulation yields powerful advantages when used for robot policies, including gracefully handling multimodal action distributions, being suitable for high-dimensional action spaces, and exhibiting impressive training stability. To fully unlock the potential of diffusion models for visuomotor policy learning on physical robots, this paper presents a set of key technical contributions including the incorporation of receding horizon control, visual conditioning, and the time-series diffusion transformer. {"arxiv_id":"2611.12202","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Tue, 10 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.12202"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":40,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2611.12202v1 Announce Type: cross \nAbstract: Involving patients' lived experience (LE) early in neurorehabilitation technology design can improve the relevance and effectiveness of solutions, yet LE experts are often involved only when finished prototypes are tested. We present and evaluate a participatory design (PD) workshop for early LE involvement, examine how LE contributions influence design processes and outcomes, and provide recommendations for similar approaches. We conducted a PD workshop at the 6th International Conference on NeuroRehabilitation. Five people who have had a stroke (LE experts) and 18 workshop attendees (including the LE experts' caregivers) were organized into five groups. Following the Discover, Define, and Develop phases of the Double Diamond model, each group used Journey Maps and Data Collection Notebooks to co-create a solution for an objective specified by an LE expert. Journey Maps were thematically analyzed, and group audio transcripts underwent structured extraction using a large language model. LE input shifted discussions from discipline-based assumptions toward priorities grounded in lived experience, including fear, confidence, sensory discomfort, fatigue, aesthetics, and independence. Narrow objectives, such as opening a blister pack, produced task-specific solutions, whereas broader objectives generated device concepts, including sensory feedback for cycling and a stimulation-equipped cooking splint. Satisfaction was high among attendees and LE experts. All workshop tools and protocols are shared to support adoption. The workshop offers a practical foundation for involving LE experts early in neurorehabilitation technology development. Future iterations should better capture psychological and social dimensions, allow more reflection, and include the full range of relevant stakeholders through sustained transdisciplinary engagement between researchers and the LE community.","title":"Co-Creating Neurorehabilitation Technology Alongside Lived Experience Experts: A Participatory Design Workshop","title_en":"Co-Creating Neurorehabilitation Technology Alongside Lived Experience Experts: A Participatory Design Workshop","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12202","version":null,"version_updated_at":null}

{"arxiv_id":"2506.06361","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Tue, 10 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2506.06361"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":80,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2506.06361v4 Announce Type: replace \nAbstract: Tactile perception has the potential to significantly enhance dexterous robotic manipulation by providing rich local information that can complement or substitute for other sensory modalities such as vision. However, tactile sensing is an inherently local sensor modality, providing information only at the points of contact. This strict locality necessitates the use of active perception techniques to acquire useful, task-relevant information from manipulated objects or the environment in general. Hence, the agent must actively guide sensors toward regions with more informative or significant features and integrate this information over time to understand a scene or complete a task. While active perception and tactile sensing methods have received significant attention recently, both fields lack standardized benchmarks. To bridge this gap, we introduce the Tactile MNIST Benchmark Suite, an open-source, Gymnasium-compatible benchmark specifically designed for active tactile perception tasks, including classification, localization, pose estimation, and volume estimation. Our benchmark suite offers diverse simulation scenarios, from simple toy environments to complex tactile perception tasks using vision-based tactile sensors. Furthermore, we offer a comprehensive dataset comprising 13,580 synthetic 3D MNIST digit models and 153,600 real-world tactile samples collected from 600 3D-printed digits. Using this dataset, we train a CycleGAN for realistic tactile simulation rendering. By providing standardized protocols and reproducible evaluation frameworks, our benchmark suite facilitates systematic progress in tactile sensing and active perception more broadly.","title":"Tactile MNIST: Benchmarking Active Tactile Perception","title_en":"Tactile MNIST: Benchmarking Active Tactile Perception","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.06361","version":null,"version_updated_at":null}

{"arxiv_id":"2611.10748","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Tue, 10 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.10748"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":70,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2611.10748v1 Announce Type: new \nAbstract: Agent harnesses -- runtime scaffolds that wrap an LLM's reasoning loop with tool dispatch, verification, and persistent memory -- have become the standard substrate for deploying LLMs as autonomous agents, as demonstrated by Claude Code and Codex in software engineering. In trajectory planning, however, this paradigm has not taken hold: existing LLM-based trajectory planning methods either keep the LLM in the decision loop, exceeding the millisecond-level control budget, or offload it to offline rules or training-time supervision -- leaving the runtime planner non-evolving. Intermediate hybrids still lack the verification-and-consolidation loop that makes harnesses reliable. We ask: what runtime harness would let an LLM planner meet real-time constraints while self-evolving into a deployable one? We propose REINS, a harness built on three LLM-planner couplings: LLM outputs are (i) grounded to a learned variable-level dynamics model, (ii) verified via calibrated predicates and forward rollout, and (iii) consolidated into an indexed rule memory that serves future scenes in O(log n) without re-invoking the LLM. The harness closes a self-evolution loop: familiar scenes resolve by memory lookup; novel scenes invoke the LLM, whose verified outputs enrich the memory. {"arxiv_id":"2610.18699","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Mon, 09 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2610.18699"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":70,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2610.18699v2 Announce Type: replace \nAbstract: Evaluating robot policies before deployment typically requires producing new trajectories through real-world execution, simulators, or learned world models. These rollout-based approaches impose infrastructure requirements; simulator and world-model evaluators additionally face prediction errors that can compound over the evaluation horizon. In this paper, we study off-policy evaluation as an alternative to rollout-based robot-policy evaluation methods. Specifically, we introduce RoboFQE, an evaluator that estimates the discounted expected return of a target policy from offline robot trajectories without estimating a behavior-policy density, combining fitted Q-evaluation with a pretrained vision foundation model and learned terminal success annotation to bridge the gap between standard OPE benchmarks and continuous-control visual manipulation. Controlled experiments across simulated and real-world manipulation tasks show that RoboFQE produces accurate discounted-return estimates and preserves policy rankings even on long-horizon manipulation tasks where video world-model evaluators are degraded by autoregressive prediction errors. Ablation experiments show that pretrained vision encoders substantially outperform from-scratch alternatives, particularly on long-horizon tasks, and that learned terminal success annotation enables evaluation without ground-truth reward labels with only slight reduction of accuracy.","title":"RoboFQE: Rollout-Free Evaluation of Visual Robot Policies from Offline Trajectories","title_en":"RoboFQE: Rollout-Free Evaluation of Visual Robot Policies from Offline Trajectories","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.18699","version":null,"version_updated_at":null}

{"arxiv_id":"2611.10280","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Tue, 10 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.10280"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":40,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2611.10280v1 Announce Type: new \nAbstract: A robot that keeps learning after deployment is corrected by several people in turn, and one of them may later ask to be removed. We show that whether the robot can forget that person depends on how people correct it. The goal of removal is the robot that would exist if the person had never been there, which we compute exactly in two simulated tasks with scripted users. When users correct the robot by taking over control, an ordered log of training updates is enough: retraining on the remaining sessions in their original order gives a robot as close to the goal as training noise allows. Deleting the person's data and retraining in one pass does not, even when the other users' corrections do not depend on the removed person, because it loses the order of training. When users only nudge the robot's action, the other users' corrections carry the removed person's influence, and no method we tested recovers the goal robot. Continuing to train without the person removes most of their habits, but not what their data in the training buffer keep alive. {"arxiv_id":"2611.12806","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Tue, 10 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.12806"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":["diffusion_policy","vla"],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":80,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2611.12806v1 Announce Type: new \nAbstract: Tactile sensing is an indispensable modality for contact-rich dexterous manipulation, a capability that hints at the ultimate frontiers of embodied intelligence. However, commercially available tactile sensors are still at a relatively early stage of development, with each type of sensor offering irreplaceable strengths alongside its own drawbacks. A key challenge is thus to free tactile understanding from sensor-specific physics, so that embodied models can effectively leverage heterogeneous tactile data. To this end, we develop LingBot-Touch, a tactile foundation model characterized by the following properties. (i) Our model yields a unified representation across different tactile sensors (i.e., piezoresistive, magnetic, and visuotactile sensors), and is easily extensible to new sensor types. (ii) The resulting tactile tokens are plug-and-play: they can be seamlessly integrated into policy models across paradigms, from diffusion policy to vision-language-action (VLA) models such as $\\pi_{0.5}$ and LingBot-VLA, consistently enhancing manipulation dexterity. (iii) Extensive experiments, spanning simulation and real-robot deployments across multiple hardware platforms, demonstrate that our tactile representation substantially benefits complex manipulation tasks while maintaining strong computational efficiency. {"arxiv_id":"2611.09490","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Mon, 09 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.09490"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":50,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2611.09490v1 Announce Type: new \nAbstract: Non-contact fruit sizing from RGB-D imagery reaches sub-centimetre accuracy on workstation hardware, but in-field grading requires the same pipeline to run on a low-power single-board computer, and the cost of that transition is rarely reported. We deploy a curvature-aware cucumber length-measurement pipeline (YOLO26n detection, prompt-based segmentation and a medial arc spline estimator) on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano and a Raspberry Pi 4, and characterize both against an RTX 3050 Ti workstation by replaying 50 identical greenhouse captures of 7 specimens, with specimen-level cluster-bootstrap statistics. Accuracy is preserved: mean absolute error (MAE) is 0.58 cm (95% CI 0.46-0.69) on both the workstation and the Jetson at matched precision, with a paired difference of zero. TensorRT FP16 compilation cuts Jetson detection latency 2.57x, giving two operating points on one board: 72 ms per fruit at 0.84 cm, or 2.74 s at 0.64 cm. Four ablations map the design space. For prompted segmentation backends, measurement accuracy is fixed by the backend and reproduces across platforms to within 0.01 cm, while its cost is fixed by the platform and varies 214x, so the two choices are separable. Whole-graph INT8 quantization of the NMS-free detection head fails structurally, returning no detections, because one output tensor carries both pixel coordinates and confidences; we show that no calibration strategy can avoid this. Excluding the head restores function at 1.37x. Energy per fruit is 42.2 J on the Jetson, and its 7 W mode consumes 73% more than its 15 W mode. {"arxiv_id":"2611.08449","authors":["Yu-Cheng Chou","Shihao Wang","Jin Huang","Chi-Pin Huang","Chiao-An Yang","Xianzhe Fan","Jing Wang","Zhiqi Li","Yuanguo Kuang","Ruijie Zheng","Johan Bjorck","Sifei Liu","Hang Su","Abhishek Badki","Lei Zhang","Alan Yuille","Linxi \"Jim'' Fan","Jan Kautz","Zhiding Yu"],"categories":["cs.RO","cs.CV"],"claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.08449"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"arxiv_first_submission","published_at":"2026-11-05T18:44:43Z","rule_score":50,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"Models for physical AI tasks, such as robotics and autonomous driving, need not reason solely in language. They can use visual plans--points, bounding boxes, and trajectories--to represent spatial goals and anticipate motion. However, autoregressive vision-language models generate these plans one coordinate token at a time, making richer predictions increasingly costly. We introduce VFlash, a method for fast, accurate visual planning through Flash Primitive Decoding. VFlash exploits the known structure of visual primitives to predict their coordinates jointly, using a lightweight drafter that generates an entire primitive in one forward pass. The layout adapts to the primitive's type, dimensionality, and length, supporting compact boxes and long, variable-length trajectories. Crucially, spatial accuracy need not require reproducing an autoregressive model's exact token sequence. VFlash therefore trains on annotated primitives and directly accepts structurally valid predictions without target-token agreement. Across the evaluated 2D and 3D robot trajectory tasks, VFlash consistently reduces prediction errors relative to autoregressive decoding. Preliminary single-rollout measurements indicate approximately 25x faster generation for 3D point motion forecasting. A world action model conditioned on VFlash plans achieves 70.2% average success across four MolmoSpaces task suites, compared with 62.6% for the baseline.","title":"VFlash: Fast, Accurate Visual Planning via Flash Primitive Decoding","title_en":"VFlash: Fast, Accurate Visual Planning via Flash Primitive Decoding","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.08449v1","version":"v1","version_updated_at":"2026-11-05T18:44:43Z"}

{"arxiv_id":"2611.11842","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Tue, 10 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.11842"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":50,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2611.11842v1 Announce Type: new \nAbstract: Connected physical systems fuse observations from robots, IoT sensors, and edge-AI modules into a shared account of the world, yet most evaluations score only the final answer or action and cannot tell whether a method attributed the evidence, updated its belief, handled contradictions, and justified its decision. We argue that shared reasoning in Connected Robotics should be evaluated as an evidence-to-belief trajectory, and introduce the Connected Robotics Evidence Graph (CREG) Benchmark to make that trajectory measurable. CREG comprises 350 deterministically generated scenarios across seven regimes (justified revision, belief preservation, relation association, contradiction onset and resolution, stale/delayed evidence, and source reliability), each exposing a normative posterior reference at every evidence prefix, validated by an independent log-odds checker and screened by a blinded expert audit. Nine representation conditions separate relation content from serialization, ordering, and metadata. Evaluating four open-weight instruction models and six transparent fusion baselines yields three findings. First, entity grounding accounts for a substantial part of the weak-model deficit. Second, deleting semantic relations costs 15.3 points of strict belief-state accuracy on relation-dependent scenarios (Holm-corrected p < 0.001), but an information-matched structured list outperforms the full graph and shuffling the graph does not hurt: relation content matters where required, while graph serialization confers no consistent advantage. Third, belief accuracy is strongly non-monotonic along the evidence sequence, with mid-trajectory failures that endpoint-only evaluation cannot detect. All scenarios, references, prompts, metrics, and analysis code are released for offline, hardware-free reproduction.","title":"A Benchmark and Layered Evaluation Protocol for Evidence-Grounded Shared Belief Updating in Connected Robotics","title_en":"A Benchmark and Layered Evaluation Protocol for Evidence-Grounded Shared Belief Updating in Connected Robotics","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.11842","version":null,"version_updated_at":null}

{"arxiv_id":"2407.16151","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Tue, 10 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2407.16151"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":70,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2407.16151v2 Announce Type: replace \nAbstract: Camera pose estimation from 3D-2D correspondences is fundamental to robotics. Three practical considerations motivate this work. First, point and line features provide complementary geometric information, motivating a unified estimator. Second, the number and composition of available features vary across scenarios, requiring support for minimal and arbitrary non-minimal configurations. Third, modern visual front ends extract abundant features from individual images, enabling highly accurate pose estimation. We propose FUSE-PnPL, a flexible and unified camera pose estimator that is statistically consistent and asymptotically efficient. Specifically, we represent each line using two distinct points and adopt a unified image-space noise model for point and line measurements. By employing Pl\\\"{u}cker coordinates for line parameterization, we explicitly characterize the propagation of image endpoint noise into line residuals and formulate a joint maximum likelihood (ML) estimation problem for combined point and line measurements. To efficiently solve this problem, FUSE-PnPL employs a two-stage estimation scheme. First, noise variance estimation and bias elimination yield a consistent initial pose estimate. A single Gauss-Newton iteration then refines this estimate, achieving asymptotic efficiency as its mean squared error asymptotically attains the Cram\\'{e}r-Rao lower bound. Moreover, the proposed estimator has linear computational complexity with respect to the number of correspondences, making it suitable for high-precision and real-time robot pose estimation. Extensive experiments on synthetic data and real-world benchmarks validate the theoretical properties of FUSE-PnPL and demonstrate its advantages in both static global localization and dynamic SLAM systems.","title":"FUSE-PnPL: Flexible, Unified, Statistically Consistent, and Asymptotically Efficient Camera Pose Estimation from Points and Lines","title_en":"FUSE-PnPL: Flexible, Unified, Statistically Consistent, and Asymptotically Efficient Camera Pose Estimation from Points and Lines","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.16151","version":null,"version_updated_at":null}

{"arxiv_id":"2611.11050","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Tue, 10 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.11050"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":50,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2611.11050v1 Announce Type: new \nAbstract: Designing real-time control for nonlinear systems to track periodic orbits can be challenging, especially for complex and coupled dynamical systems (e.g., tethered kites), where the true model parameters are hard to obtain. To address this, we propose a physics-informed Koopman learning approach that incorporates periodic-orbit stability directly into the learned linear predictor. The approach combines the underlying periodic structure of the dynamics along with periodic state-input trajectory data to learn physically consistent linear predictors (in lifted/observable space). We leverage Floquet theory, which studies the stability of periodic orbits in nonlinear systems, to obtain the periodic stability information of a given orbit via a monodromy matrix (i.e., the state transition matrix over an entire period). Subsequently, we impose open-loop monodromy constraints to learn Floquet-parameterized linear predictors using a least-squares Extended Dynamic Mode Decomposition (EDMD) formulation, thereby constraining the search space and aiding in Koopman learning. We then utilize these linear predictors to design a model predictive control (MPC) law for tracking periodic references. Finally, we evaluate the designed framework on a cartpole system under periodic forcing and compare it against a purely data-driven baseline.","title":"Floquet-Parameterized Koopman-MPC for Tracking Periodic Orbits","title_en":"Floquet-Parameterized Koopman-MPC for Tracking Periodic Orbits","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.11050","version":null,"version_updated_at":null}

The standard rule uses one fixed clipping range for all samples. While this choice offers simplicity and effectiveness, it fails to distinguish statistically harmful extreme ratio values from large, yet tolerable changes. We study how to adapt the clipping radius to the reliability of the induced importance ratio distribution. Our case study demonstrates that reliable updates require controlling these extreme ratios, rather than merely verifying that individual ratios fall within a fixed interval. Motivated by this observation, we propose Ordered Policy Optimization (\\textsc{OPO}). In each minibatch, \\textsc{OPO} sorts the importance ratios, selects the extreme ratios that potentially have the largest effect on the update, and assigns them adaptive sample-wise radii instead of using the fixed clipping radius. These radii are derived from a prescribed tail profile, which specifies desired target values for the selected extreme ratios. The resulting objective remains first-order and requires only minibatch sorting and a modified policy loss. Experiments conducted on MuJoCo and Atari benchmarks demonstrate that this simple modification achieves strong performance relative to established baselines.","title":"Ordered Policy Optimization","title_en":"Ordered Policy Optimization","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.08936","version":null,"version_updated_at":null}

In conventional Euclidean-distance-based frontier pipelines, geometric distance may poorly represent the actual collision-free travel cost in cluttered environments, leading to inefficient frontier choices. This paper presents a lightweight path-aware frontier re-ranking method for LiDAR-based UAV exploration. The method first retains a small top-N set of promising frontier candidates using a lightweight utility function and then applies time-bounded RRT* planning to estimate their feasible path costs for re-ranking. The path generated for the selected frontier is further reused for navigation to reduce redundant global planning. Experiments in three warehouse-like environments show that the proposed method consistently produces shorter exploration trajectories than conventional frontier baselines, with traveled-distance reductions of up to 14.1%, while reducing exploration time by up to 9.5% in two environments and remaining competitive in the third. {"arxiv_id":"2603.16861","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Tue, 10 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2603.16861"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":80,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2603.16861v3 Announce Type: replace \nAbstract: A prevailing view in robot learning is that simulation alone is not enough; effective sim-to-real transfer is widely believed to require at least some real-world data collection or task-specific fine-tuning to bridge the gap between simulated and physical environments. We challenge that assumption. With sufficiently large-scale and diverse simulated synthetic training data, we show that zero-shot transfer to the real world is not only possible, but effective for both static and mobile manipulation. We introduce MolmoBot-Engine, a fully open-source pipeline for procedural data generation across robots, tasks, and diverse simulated environments in MolmoSpaces. With it, we release MolmoBot-Data, a dataset of 1.7 million expert trajectories for articulated object manipulation and pick-and-place tasks. We train three policy classes: MolmoBot, a Molmo2-based multi-frame vision-language model with a flow-matching action head; MolmoBot-Pi0, which replicates the $\\pi_0$ architecture to enable direct comparison; and MolmoBot-SPOC, a lightweight policy suitable for edge deployment and amenable to RL fine-tuning. We evaluate on two robotic platforms: the Franka FR3 for tabletop manipulation tasks and the Rainbow Robotics RB-Y1 mobile manipulator for door opening, drawer manipulation, cabinet interaction, and mobile pick-and-place. Without any real-world fine-tuning, our policies achieve zero-shot transfer to unseen objects and environments. On tabletop pick-and-place, MolmoBot achieves a success rate of 79.2% in real world evaluations across 4 settings, outperforming $\\pi_{0.5}$ at 39.2%. Our results demonstrate that procedural environment generation combined with diverse articulated assets can produce robust manipulation policies that generalize broadly to the real world. Technical website: https://allenai.github.io/MolmoBot","title":"MolmoB0T: Large-Scale Simulation Enables Zero-Shot Manipulation","title_en":"MolmoB0T: Large-Scale Simulation Enables Zero-Shot Manipulation","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.16861","version":null,"version_updated_at":null}

{"arxiv_id":"2611.05119","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Mon, 09 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.05119"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":70,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2611.05119v2 Announce Type: replace \nAbstract: Dexterous manipulation involves not only moving objects, but also arranging the hand around them to maintain useful contacts and enable subsequent actions. Yet many learning-based systems specify goals primarily through object poses or trajectories, leaving hand-object configurations to emerge implicitly. We introduce DexHOT, which formulates dexterous manipulation as hand-object configuration transfer: moving between feasible configurations that jointly specify hand articulation and object pose relative to the wrist. DexHOT learns a reusable relation-conditioned transfer primitive from synthetic feasible configuration pairs, without human reference motions, and composes long-horizon behaviors through closed-loop tracking of configuration subgoals. On DexHOTBench with 120 objects, a single policy achieves 80.5% transfer success on seen objects and 69.4% on unseen objects; on a real dexterous hand, it achieves 61.5% success over 200 real-robot transfers and 90% task success across six demonstration-guided tasks. These results show that explicit hand-object goals provide an expressive and composable interface for dexterous manipulation. More details and videos are available at https://dex-hot.github.io/.","title":"DexHOT: Learning Hand-Object Configuration Transfer for Dexterous Manipulation","title_en":"DexHOT: Learning Hand-Object Configuration Transfer for Dexterous Manipulation","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05119","version":null,"version_updated_at":null}

{"arxiv_id":"2611.11489","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Tue, 10 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.11489"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":80,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2611.11489v1 Announce Type: new \nAbstract: Autonomous UAV exploration is increasingly used for large-scale surveying and inspection in inaccessible or disaster-affected environments, where onboard memory and computational resources are often severely constrained. Most existing UAV exploration systems maintain globally queryable geometric map representations for motion planning and exploration decision-making, causing memory consumption and spatial-query costs to increase with the explored area. Robot-centric local mapping bounds dense-map memory and computation but discards global task context needed for long-horizon exploration.We present FLAVOR, a hierarchical spatio-temporal framework that confines dense metric geometry to a robot-centric local map while retaining compact global observation and task context. At the observation level, lightweight LiDAR-keyframe visibility records preserve ray-wise evidence for frontier reasoning. At the task level, unresolved frontiers beyond the local-map extent are retained as compact pending tasks associated with odometry anchors. A sparse topological graph connects these anchors through retained routes for future revisits.Upon returning to a task region, FLAVOR reconstructs the frontier and exploration viewpoint from observations, while the topological route is instantiated and validated against the current local map before execution. Dense-map capacity remains fixed as exploration expands, with exploration-dependent memory growth confined to compact observation and task context.FLAVOR achieves 31.98--41.88% shorter exploration time and a 94--99% smaller map memory footprint than the best baseline that completes all three simulated scenes. In real-world deployments, it reduces this footprint by 92.67% in the forest and 62.42% at the construction site relative to an explicit point-cloud ikd-tree while preserving long-term task continuity under constrained onboard resources.","title":"Beyond Memory Limits: A Hierarchical Spatio-Temporal Map Representation for Large-Scale 3D Autonomous Exploration","title_en":"Beyond Memory Limits: A Hierarchical Spatio-Temporal Map Representation for Large-Scale 3D Autonomous Exploration","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.11489","version":null,"version_updated_at":null}

{"arxiv_id":"2607.24852","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Mon, 09 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2607.24852"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":50,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2607.24852v5 Announce Type: replace-cross \nAbstract: Photogrammetric reconstructions used for inspection are often delivered without an independent accuracy check. Hold-out self-validation is a possible substitute. Images are withheld, their orientations are re-estimated from the rest of the block, and agreement is taken as evidence of quality. We test it on ten GNSS-referenced aerial captures from eight sites, on ETH3D and EuRoC, and on 30 IMC 2025 scenes. The standard form re-localises each withheld image only against points seen by at least two retained images. Its score saturates. It stayed at 1.00 in all 40 thinned reconstructions while camera-position error varied by a factor of up to 5.9 within one capture. It also scored 1.00 on a corrupted model with only one of 226 cameras within 5 m. Reprojection error ranked some of the worst models best. A few lost cameras can raise the least-squares RMSE to the size of the block, so we also evaluate with a robust alignment. Taking the correspondences from the verified matches lowered the score below 0.95 in 14 of 18 corrupted runs, against 4 for the standard form and 10 when its failed resections count as errors, with all seven nominal runs at 1.00. Mapping the block again without the withheld images also responds, but mapping the same corrupted data twice without withholding gave a similar disagreement, so the signal is mainly that a corrupted reconstruction is not reproducible. Neither test can see an error that every reconstruction repeats, and neither can replace check points.","title":"Hold-Out Self-Validation Cannot Certify the Accuracy of Photogrammetric Reconstructions","title_en":"Hold-Out Self-Validation Cannot Certify the Accuracy of Photogrammetric Reconstructions","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24852","version":null,"version_updated_at":null}

{"arxiv_id":"2606.24450","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Mon, 09 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2606.24450"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":["reinforcement_learning"],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":80,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2606.24450v2 Announce Type: replace \nAbstract: Perceiving physical contact is fundamental to dexterous manipulation. While robots often rely on dedicated hardware tactile sensors, humans exhibit a remarkable ability to infer contact by integrating visual information with an innate sense of their body's pose and movement. Inspired by this embodied perceptual skill, we investigate whether a robot can learn to infer contact from vision, an approach that also offers a scalable alternative to tactile hardware specifically for binary contact estimation, which faces practical challenges in cost, fragility, and integration. We present NoContactNoWorries, a transformer-based multimodal framework that fuses RGB-D vision with the robot's proprioception to infer binary contact states as a pseudo-tactile signal for hand-object interactions. We validate by training a single contact prediction model on multiple objects and show that the inferred contact signal supports downstream reinforcement learning agents for in-hand object reorientation, generalizing to novel objects. {"arxiv_id":"2611.10699","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Tue, 10 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.10699"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":50,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2611.10699v1 Announce Type: cross \nAbstract: While 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) is typically optimized from images only, many robotics and mapping applications provide both camera and high-definition LiDAR data, combining rich visual appearance with accurate geometric structure. We introduce PLS-GS, a probabilistic LiDAR scaffold for Gaussian Splatting that exploits this complementary sensing setting to construct a compact 3DGS representation aligned to the measured surface. PLS-GS fits a Hierarchical Gaussian Mixture Model jointly over position and color, yielding a continuous and adaptive scaffold that eliminates the need for discrete scene partitioning such as voxel grids or octrees. The fitted mixture then guides the renderable 3DGS Gaussians: each rendering Gaussian is associated with a GMM component and constrained in the local surface frame induced by that component's covariance. A Mahalanobis support loss bounds the deviation of the rendering Gaussians from the corresponding LiDAR-derived surface. Across five large outdoor scenes, PLS-GS places primitives markedly closer to the LiDAR measurements than both image- and LiDAR-initialized baselines, while employing substantially fewer primitives, yielding a considerably more compact model and faster rendering. At matched capacity, PLS-GS places primitives closer to the LiDAR measurements, with comparable rendering quality. {"arxiv_id":"2611.10107","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Tue, 10 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.10107"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":60,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2611.10107v1 Announce Type: new \nAbstract: Enabling robots to infer interaction-relevant physical properties from vision before contact would improve planning and control in unstructured environments. Vision provides useful pre-contact information, but appearance alone is often ambiguous: visually similar regions can induce different friction, stiffness, or sinkage responses upon contact. Existing approaches often collapse this ambiguity to a point estimate or aggregate experience through fixed semantic classes, limiting their ability to preserve distinct physical regimes. Instead, we propose a real-time estimator that replaces semantic class indexing with an interaction-grounded Gaussian-mixture posterior over latent physical parameters, conditioned directly on continuous visual embeddings. Our approach maintains interaction-derived Gaussian parameter estimates, typically from inverse modeling, as mixture components while using embedding similarity to retrieve and weight relevant past interactions for each new query region. A support-aware fusion mechanism incorporates a conditional generative prior model when interaction history is sparse, while a learned embedding refinement improves retrieval relevance without discretizing the representation. Our experiments show that the estimator recovers multimodal physical beliefs, rejects unrelated interaction history, avoids spatial map discretization, and evaluates at controller rates. {"arxiv_id":"2611.12526","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Tue, 10 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.12526"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":60,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2611.12526v1 Announce Type: new \nAbstract: Multi-sensor state estimation requires accurate spatial and temporal calibration between heterogeneous sensors. Existing spatiotemporal calibration methods typically represent sensor extrinsic parameters as a rigid-body transformation together with a scalar temporal offset, causing the spatial and temporal parameters to enter the estimation problem through separate mechanisms. While the spatial transformation composes directly with the robot pose, accounting for the temporal offset requires evaluating the trajectory at a shifted time, typically through motion compensation, interpolation, or a continuous-time trajectory representation. In this work, we formulate joint trajectory estimation and spatiotemporal calibration using the special Galilean group for the robot trajectory and the Aristotelian subgroup for sensor extrinsics. This representation incorporates the coupling between motion and temporal offset directly through the group structure, avoiding the need for a separately parameterized continuous-time trajectory. We develop twist- and IMU-driven motion priors, accommodate both ideal and non-ideal clocks, and evaluate the framework with camera, position, and range measurements. Simulated and real experiments demonstrate calibration and trajectory-estimation performance comparable to established methods across heterogeneous sensor configurations. {"arxiv_id":"2611.10660","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Tue, 10 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.10660"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":60,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2611.10660v1 Announce Type: cross \nAbstract: Latent world models enable visual control by planning action sequences in compact representation spaces, but a gap remains between how latent dynamics are learned and how they are used for planning. First, teacher-forced training does not expose the dynamics model to the recursively predicted latent states encountered during planning. Second, sampling-based planners typically initialize action search from goal-agnostic proposals, without exploiting the action-conditioned dynamics learned by the world model. We introduce Dynamics-Informed Action Learning (DIAL) to bridge these two gaps. During training, rollout alignment exposes the forward model to its own autoregressive latent predictions, while multi-step inverse supervision trains a lightweight inverse dynamics head to infer actions from latent-state transitions. We further apply the inverse head to model-generated transitions with its parameters held fixed, encouraging predicted rollouts to retain action-relevant information. At test time, DIAL autoregressively couples the inverse and forward dynamics to construct a dynamics-informed action sequence toward the goal, which initializes the mean of the Cross-Entropy Method (CEM) proposal distribution. The subsequent CEM search then refines this initialization using the standard sampling and updating procedure. {"arxiv_id":"2611.11087","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Tue, 10 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.11087"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":60,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2611.11087v1 Announce Type: cross \nAbstract: We present SoftPAT3D, a physics-augmented framework for text-to-3D scene generation in which deformable objects, such as cloth, stuffed toys and ropes, are generated as physically valid, simulation-ready bodies and placed in intersection-free contact with the furniture that supports them, with one another and with themselves. Existing physics-augmented pipelines simulate rigid bodies only and cannot accommodate a generated deformable object, which text-to-3D generation returns as a geometrically invalid mesh, sometimes self-intersecting, that has no rest shape, no material model and no admissible initial state. These are the inputs a deformable simulation requires, and we construct each from information already in the pipeline. The rest shape comes from how the object is manufactured rather than from the generated physically inconsistent deformed configuration, and a material library assigns each deformable object its initial elastic parameters, which can then be optimized. The occluded support is regenerated and converted into a watertight collision mesh, each object is released from an optimizable placement above the supporting part that the prompt specifies, and the complete scene is driven to static equilibrium under one unified contact model, with completion verified by geometric checks and a vision-language model. When a scene fails the prompt, a grid search over placements corrects it, and the adjoint of a differentiable simulation of the same contact energy reaches the targets the grid does not, places several bodies jointly and recovers and optimizes material parameters. Multi-body scenes equilibrate in a single simulation, and the pipeline also runs from the text prompt alone. Existing physics-augmented pipelines simulate rigid bodies only and cannot accommodate a generated deformable object, which text-to-3D generation returns as a geometrically invalid mesh, sometimes self-intersecting, that has no rest shape, no material model and no admissible initial state. These are the inputs a deformable simulation requires, and we construct each from information already in the pipeline. The rest shape comes from how the object is manufactured rather than from the generated physically inconsistent deformed configuration, and a material library assigns each deformable object its initial elastic parameters, which can then be optimized. The occluded support is regenerated and converted into a watertight collision mesh, each object is released from an optimizable placement above the supporting part that the prompt specifies, and the complete scene is driven to static equilibrium under one unified contact model, with completion verified by geometric checks and a vision-language model. When a scene fails the prompt, a grid search over placements corrects it, and the adjoint of a differentiable simulation of the same contact energy reaches the targets the grid does not, places several bodies jointly and recovers and optimizes material parameters. Multi-body scenes equilibrate in a single simulation, and the pipeline also runs from the text prompt alone. We systematically investigate five auxiliary tasks---person segmentation, bounding-box grounding, visual-spatial classification (VSC), future DINO feature prediction, and future-frame prediction---and adopt complementary mask and bounding-box supervision to enhance target delineation and localization. {"arxiv_id":"2611.10566","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Tue, 10 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.10566"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":70,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2611.10566v1 Announce Type: new \nAbstract: LiDAR-based localization and mapping systems produce registered point clouds that serve as geometric measurements for downstream estimation and navigation. Registration errors introduce duplicated surfaces and structural deformation into these measurements. In the absence of an independent reference, online assessment relies on geometry accumulated from earlier measurements. Such assessment requires tolerance to sampling variation and an accumulation process in which observations enter the history only after evaluation. We therefore formulate a recursive Bayesian comparison that couples geometric assessment with history maintenance. A Normal-Inverse-Wishart model represents historical voxel geometry and its uncertainty, while a weak isotropic reference adapts to current sampling. Comparing the marginal predictive support of the same current points under both models yields Normalized Drift Evidence (NDE). Assessment precedes assimilation: positive NDE triggers an alarm and preserves the preceding historical state; otherwise, the current observations update the history. Across 14 real-world sequences totaling approximately 73 min from four platform types, alarms identified all nine corrupted sequences and were absent from all five consistent sequences. In four representative scenarios with event references, first alarms occurred within 0.9 s of the reference times, with no preceding alarms. Cross-backend evaluation demonstrates consistent responses to reconstructed geometry. Ablation and controlled perturbation results establish the roles of uncertainty modeling, recursive history, displacement, and geometric support. Mean processing time is 4.2--6.1 ms per update at 1 Hz. In ten UAV trials, alarms initiated odometry isolation, landing, relocalization, and mission continuation.","title":"Online Geometric Consistency Assessment of LiDAR Measurements via Recursive Bayesian Comparison","title_en":"Online Geometric Consistency Assessment of LiDAR Measurements via Recursive Bayesian Comparison","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.10566","version":null,"version_updated_at":null}

{"arxiv_id":"2611.12818","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Tue, 10 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.12818"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":["reinforcement_learning"],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":60,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2611.12818v1 Announce Type: new \nAbstract: In ultrasound-guided femoral access, probe pressure deforms the tissue and changes the vascular anatomy a robot observes. A simulator must reproduce these mechanics fast enough for robotic interaction, yet the computational effort needed for a clinically meaningful signal like vein collapse before artery is unclear. We test the feasibility of a physics-based simulation in NVIDIA's Isaac Sim for Healthcare, with Stable Neo-Hookean tissue solved by Vertex Block Descent on one GPU. A simulation of a low-fidelity cylindrical benchtop phantom with known geometry and mechanical properties, pressed by a robot, predicted its artery within 5 percentage points at every depth. It matched the vein within 3 points through 11 mm of a 25.4 mm press and followed the collapse behavior of the low-fidelity physical phantom. Across element size, time step, and solver iterations, wall clock time per frame scaled linearly with solver work, but accuracy did not improve with more work. The chosen setting reduced solver time per frame by a factor of 976, from 29,700 ms to 30.4 ms, while remaining within 1.03 points of the finest reference setting. The physics solver alone took 30.4 ms per frame, while the full stack, including ultrasound and graphics rendering, took 56.4 ms per frame. Finally, when seeded with realistic literature-based mechanical properties, the digital leg model compressed the vein far more than the artery at every setting, reproducing the expected clinical signal of vein collapse before artery, which is used to distinguish them. In total, these results suggest that the NVIDIA Isaac Sim platform may be suitable for augmenting reinforcement learning training or online simulation for autonomous femoral access with ultrasound.","title":"Simulating Vein Compressibility for Ultrasound-Guided Femoral Access: Speed, Accuracy, and Phantom Validation","title_en":"Simulating Vein Compressibility for Ultrasound-Guided Femoral Access: Speed, Accuracy, and Phantom Validation","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12818","version":null,"version_updated_at":null}
