{"arxiv_id":"2611.11854","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Tue, 10 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.11854"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":["vla"],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":80,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2611.11854v1 Announce Type: new \nAbstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models pair a vision-language backbone with an action head, but in closed-loop control the backbone sits on the control-critical path: while it computes, the robot keeps moving, so each executed action is conditioned on an increasingly stale observation. A larger backbone therefore directly blocks reactivity, especially in humanoid dexterous manipulation. We present DASH, a Decoupled Asynchronous System for Humanoids that removes this coupling. DASH splits the policy into a slow vision-language model (System 2) and a fast flow-matching action head (System 1) that run as concurrent processes over the LCM communication protocol, so the control rate is set by the action head alone, independent of backbone size. The action head fuses stale semantics from a frozen backbone with fresh vision from its own ResNet encoder, desynchronized training exposes it to the staleness it meets at deployment, and an adaptive temporal aggregator aligns overlapping action chunks under variable inference latency. On an asynchronous RoboTwin benchmark that charges inference latency in simulated time, DASH holds 20 Hz control rate from 0.8B to 8B backbones while the synchronous rate falls from 9.7 to 4.1 Hz, with higher success at every size. On a real humanoid with dexterous hands, DASH achieves clearly higher pick-and-place success than the synchronous pipeline.","title":"Decoupled Asynchronous System for Humanoids (DASH): Latency-Agnostic Scaling of Vision-Language-Action Models for Humanoid Manipulation","title_en":"Decoupled Asynchronous System for Humanoids (DASH): Latency-Agnostic Scaling of Vision-Language-Action Models for Humanoid Manipulation","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.11854","version":null,"version_updated_at":null}

## ⚠️ Breaking changes (v0.6.1 -> v0.7.0)

v0.7.0 rebuilds installation, training, inference and the hardware layer. A few changes need your attention when upgrading:

**Installation**
- On Linux, `torch` and `torchvision` now come from PyPI as CUDA 13 builds (NVIDIA driver 580.65 or newer); the `cu128` index is gone. For older drivers, install torch from a CUDA 12 index first (see the installation guide). macOS needs 14+ (15+ for MPS).
- Pins moved: `transformers` 5.22, `huggingface-hub>=1.31, < 3`, `motorbridge` 0.5, `datasets < 6`, `Pillow < 14`, `torchcodec < 0.18`.

**Training**
- Weights & Biases is replaced by Trackio (the `training` extra installs `trackio`): `--wandb.*` is now `--trackio.*`, `entity`/`mode` have no equivalent, remote jobs with tracking need `--trackio.space_id`, and checkpoints are no longer uploaded as artifacts by default.
- FSDP1 is replaced by FSDP2/HSDP (`--parallelism.dp_shard`, `--parallelism.dp_replicate`, `--accelerator.*`); mixed precision is set with `--accelerator.mixed_precision`. FSDP checkpoints saved with lerobot ≤ 0.6.x cannot be resumed (their `model.safetensors` still loads), and Accelerate YAML/env configuration is rejected unless `LEROBOT_ALLOW_ACCELERATE_ENV=1`.
- `--policy.use_peft=true` alone now trains LoRA instead of silently fully fine-tuning.
- Image transforms are batched: `GaussianNoise`, `MotionBlur`, `GaussianPatchBrightness`, `RandomShadow`, `CoarseDropout`, `GammaCorrection` and `PlanckianJitter` were silent no-ops on uint8 frames and now apply. `ImageTransforms` takes tensors only; the per-sample classes are deprecated.

**Inference & rollout**
- `lerobot.async_inference` and `lerobot[async]` are removed: use `lerobot[remote]`, `lerobot-policy-server` and `lerobot-rollout --inference.type=remote`. `lerobot.rollout.inference` moved to `lerobot.inference`.
- `select_action` / `predict_action_chunk` may return a `PolicyOutput` (`{"action", "prediction"}`) instead of a bare tensor; use `policy_output_to_transition` when calling them directly.
- With `--interpolation_multiplier>1`, rollout strategies record one frame per policy action instead of one per tick.

**Simulation & environments**
- `lerobot.envs. ` moved to `lerobot.sim.integrations. `, env configs are named `*EnvConfig` (`LiberoEnv` -> `LiberoEnvConfig`), and in-process envs return canonical observations (HWC uint8 images, flat float32 state; map camera names with `--rename_map`). `--env.type` is unchanged.
- Removed env fields: Aloha/PushT `observation_height`/`observation_width`, MetaWorld `episode_length`/`multitask_eval`, RoboTwin `obs_type`/`render_mode`. MetaWorld's default task is `metaworld-push-v3`.
- EnvHub `make_env` is called without `cfg` and must return an unwrapped `SyncVectorEnv`/`AsyncVectorEnv` unless `--env.use_native_batch=true`.

**Policies**
- `dtype` is the single precision key of every policy config; `torch_dtype`, `vlm_dtype`, `model_params_fp32` and `model_dtype` are ignored or removed. In Python pass `torch.bfloat16`, not a string.
- MolmoAct2: `enable_lora_vlm`, `enable_lora_action_expert` and `train_action_expert_only` are replaced by `--policy.train_mode_vlm={fft,lora,freeze}`; `action_mode` defaults to `continuous`.
- EO1: `chunk_size` and `n_action_steps` default to 16.
- VLA-JEPA: checkpoints trained before the RoPE fix need `--policy.world_model_rope_legacy=true`; `binarize_gripper_action` and `pre_snap_gripper_action` default to `false`.

**Datasets**
- `--dataset.streaming=true` uses a new disk-less episode-pool reader with `--dataset.streaming_*` options; `Backtrackable` is removed.

**Hardware**
- Feetech and Dynamixel run on one rustypot-backed `SerialMotorsBus` (`lerobot[feetech]`/`[dynamixel]` install `rustypot` instead of the vendor SDKs). `FeetechMotorsBus`/`DynamixelMotorsBus` are deprecated aliases, `OperatingMode`/`TorqueMode` give way to `bus.set_operating_mode("position")`, and the control tables, `encoding_utils` and the SDK-level helpers (`broadcast_ping`, `scan_port`, ...) are removed. Calibration files are unchanged.
- reBot B601: the config is driven by `motor_family` (`dm`, `rs`); `gripper_mit_kp`/`gripper_mit_kd` are removed and per-joint gains take a dict instead of a list.

Recent work conjectures that a small m suffices for feature-space world models and that a strictly proper energy score should replace the hard minimum. We test both claims with one-step world models on frozen DINOv2/v3 patch tokens, using benchmarks whose futures can be enumerated. Under mode-like uncertainty, nearest-of-m with m=16 covers the enumerated futures better than 50-step flow matching (at about 1/30 of its latency), one-step flow generators and an energy-score generator at matched parameter counts, and its rollouts stay on the token manifold where flow rollouts drift. One quantity governs the choice of m: the nearest-of-m objective is the expected distortion of a random codebook of m draws from the generator. This view yields three predictions, recorded before the corresponding runs: (i) memorization of the realized outcome in contexts that never repeat, whose strength is governed by the codebook's miss distortion I(m) rather than its miss probability, and which an energy-score generator does not escape by raising m; (ii) a flattening of mode probabilities with m, matching a known optimum within 0.01; and (iii) under-dispersion on continuous high-dimensional outcomes, which bounds the method on real robot video. Per-step matching on self-rollouts cuts long-horizon error by a third on a stochastic Push-T variant; an ablation separates its manifold and coverage benefits. Planning success does not improve despite accurate risk estimates, a negative result we report with its diagnosis.","title":"How Many Candidates Does a One-Step World Model Need? We present AHEADance, a robot-native streaming dance generator executed on a humanoid robot by a whole-body tracker. ListenAhead conditions each chunk on heard music and a frozen music model's forecasts of the coming music, aligned to their target times and weighted by reliability. The forecasts carry the timing of upcoming beats almost as well as the actual future; with them, the generator is better synchronized with the music and concentrates more motion energy at its song's beat frequency. Commit Forcing trains continuation from the model's own committed chunks, updating both the latent history and the decoded boundary of the next chunk; it reduces low activity from 83.5% to 10.3%, the level of real dance. Three music evaluators, each validated on real G1 dance, test synchronization, song and style. {"arxiv_id":"2611.12676","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Tue, 10 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.12676"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":["vla","reinforcement_learning","imitation_learning"],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":80,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2611.12676v1 Announce Type: new \nAbstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models are trained as general-purpose foundation models for robot learning, and require fine-tuning for each downstream task and robot. This raises practical questions such as how much data and training updates are needed, how checkpoints should be selected, and whether simulation can be leveraged to alleviate the cost of real data collection. We study these questions on a task that requires both precise manipulation and spatial understanding of the scene. In this task, an SO-101 arm moves a chess king between two squares that are given only by their names, such as e4 and a5. We fine-tune $\\pi_{0.5}$ with various dataset sizes and update budgets, using teleoperated demonstrations as well as simulated demonstrations from a randomized scripted expert that imitates the variability of human demonstrations. In simulation, the success rate scales with both data and updates. Importantly, we find that a short learning-rate cool-down adds up to 31 points and is necessary for comparing checkpoints, and that validation loss and action error are unreliable for model selection. On the real arm, we fine-tune on up to 256 teleoperated demonstrations and evaluate ten policies in 25 trials each. Partial results indicate that pretraining on the simulated demonstrations helps substantially, most clearly when real data is scarce. We also present a negative result, in which training on the policy's own rollouts with filtered behavior cloning, RECAP-style advantage conditioning, corrections from an automatic coach, or residual reinforcement learning did not yield a measurable improvement over plain behavior cloning in our setting. {"arxiv_id":"2611.12885","authors":["Heng Fang","Zehui Guo","Yuehan Zhang","Mingyang Du","Dingkang Liang","Xiang Bai"],"categories":["cs.CV","cs.RO"],"claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.12885"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"arxiv_first_submission","published_at":"2026-11-09T18:59:45Z","rule_score":90,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"Trained action policies write manipulation skill into network weights, tying what is learned to the distribution it is learned from. In-context learning (ICL) avoids this coupling but has not matched trained policies, because a demonstration recorded in another scene carries no feedback from the world the robot currently faces. We observe that what an agent learns in context is semantic, recording task steps and object roles rather than visual appearance, so experience gathered in one world transfers to another. Based on this insight, we propose World In-Context Learning (WICL), a paradigm in which a frozen model starts from a demonstration, rehearses the task in a world such as a simulator, and writes the feedback into its context rather than its weights. We build RoboScript, a modular infrastructure that implements WICL for agentic manipulation. From a single demonstration, RoboScript learns each task through rehearsal in simulation, freezes the learned knowledge as a Task Memory, and deploys the frozen memory on new scenes with data isolation that ensures every deployment input is available on a real robot. On all 50 tasks of RoboTwin 2.0, RoboScript reaches 83.4% mean success across clean and randomized settings with one demonstration per task and no gradient updates, exceeding the strongest trained action policy by over 20 points. The method generalizes across visual distributions, improves through reflection, scales with the foundation model, and transfers to a physical dual-arm robot through cross-embodiment memory adaptation. With a world in the loop, a robot can learn a manipulation task in its context as well as it learns one in its weights. All code is available at https://github.com/ArcheOne-AI/RoboScript","title":"World In-Context Learning for Agentic Robot Manipulation","title_en":"World In-Context Learning for Agentic Robot Manipulation","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12885v1","version":"v1","version_updated_at":"2026-11-09T18:59:45Z"}

{"arxiv_id":"2611.13311","authors":["Mahindra Rautela"],"categories":["cs.LG","cs.RO"],"claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.13311"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"arxiv_first_submission","published_at":"2026-11-09T22:24:48Z","rule_score":70,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"Flow matching robot policies commonly use a fixed Euler step count selected from offline accuracy sweeps. At inference time, however, each policy input (visual observation, robot state, and language instruction) together with a source-noise draw defines a different ODE trajectory and sequence of local Jacobians. We ask whether a step count that accurately follows the nominal noise-to-action trajectory can still be too coarse for strongly contracting directions around it. An exact two-coordinate system and a controlled augmentation of six trained flow models show that trajectory accuracy and local Euler stability can impose different step requirements even when the original learned transport is unchanged. We then study a frozen $π_{0.5}$-LIBERO checkpoint without modifying its weights or action dynamics. Across 30 policy inputs from 10 LIBERO-10 tasks, the Jacobian exhibits strong contracting directions near the action endpoint, yet no sampled mode violates the Euler non-expansion condition. On five of those inputs, accuracy sweeps require 4--9 Euler steps at 5% terminal error and 87--112 at 1%. These five paired cases are therefore consistent with accuracy-limited rather than stability-limited sampling under this local criterion, while the controlled experiments show why endpoint accuracy alone cannot rule out a separate stability requirement.","title":"One Trajectory, Two Requirements: Accuracy and Local Stability in Euler Sampling for Flow Matching Policies","title_en":"One Trajectory, Two Requirements: Accuracy and Local Stability in Euler Sampling for Flow Matching Policies","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.13311v1","version":"v1","version_updated_at":"2026-11-09T22:24:48Z"}

Jiang","Abhinav Agarwal","Andreas Hofmann","Leslie Pack Kaelbling","Russ Tedrake"],"categories":["cs.RO"],"claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.10949"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":["diffusion_policy","imitation_learning"],"publication_date_basis":"arxiv_first_submission","published_at":"2026-11-07T20:25:48Z","rule_score":80,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"The diversity of a distilled diffusion policy's outputs matters beyond how it impacts the policy's success rate. In particular, downstream applications like test-time search and policy improvement require exploration. Thus, we want to distill multi-modal demonstrators into diffusion policies which reproduce their conditional action distributions. Standard data collection for behavior cloning applies a sliding window to demonstration episodes, which pairs unique observation histories with actions. These datasets can be fit by a policy that is either multi-modal, or unimodal with high Lipschitz constant to capture a diversity of actions seen at nearby observation samples. Prior work finds that diffusion policies trained on sparse data learn the latter, memorizing one action per observation. We adapt vine sampling to behavior cloning data collection to resolve this ambiguity: at some states the demonstrator visits, query it $k$ times from exactly the same observation. However, most systems still rely on teleoperation, limiting scalability and response speed. Autonomous active GDM is challenging in unknown and cluttered environments, because the robot must simultaneously explore traversable space, map the environment, and infer the gas distribution belief from sparse chemical measurements. We address this by formulating active GDM as a next-best-trajectory informative path planning (IPP) problem and develop XIT (Exploration and Exploitation Informed Trees), a sampling-based planner that grows a single shared tree toward multiple frontier goals, coupling exploration of unresolved regions with informative gas sampling en route. XIT draws a batch of samples from an Upper Confidence Bound (UCB) information field derived from the current gas posterior and expands the tree using a cost that trades off travel effort against information acquisition. To enable plume-aware exploration, we introduce the gas frontier concept, defined as unobserved regions adjacent to high gas concentrations, and propose the Wavefront Gas Frontier Detection (WGFD) algorithm for their identification. High-fidelity simulations demonstrate the benefits of XIT in terms of GDM quality and efficiency, and a scaled real-world experiment demonstrates its practicality. {"arxiv_id":"2609.12721","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Mon, 09 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2609.12721"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":["imitation_learning"],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":70,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2609.12721v2 Announce Type: replace \nAbstract: Applying an imitation learning policy to a new manipulation task usually requires collecting new demonstrations and retraining the model, which makes sample efficiency a practical concern. Pretraining on large-scale robot datasets is effective in this respect, but such datasets are costly to collect and train on, while data augmentation techniques typically require a new round of data generation and retraining for each task. A complementary question is what useful prior can be provided to a policy at negligible cost before any task-specific data are collected. In this study, we construct a geometric visual pretraining dataset in which each scene contains only a plane, an object, and a hand, and trajectories are generated automatically. The scenes contain neither textures nor backgrounds; pretraining primarily exposes the policy to the geometric relationship between the hand and the object. Furthermore, representing the hand as a cube avoids tailoring the dataset to a specific robot morphology. We evaluate this geometric prior using ACT on three simulated robots across five manipulation tasks each, as well as on three real-world robot tasks. Across many of these robot--task combinations, fine-tuning from the geometric prior achieves higher success rates in the early stages of training than training from scratch while using only a small number of task demonstrations. This paper presents a capturability-aware sequential Model Predictive Control (MPC) framework for Linear Inverted Pendulum (LIP)-based humanoid footstep planning in the presence of obstacles. The proposed method combines obstacle avoidance with capturability constraints through safe corridors constructed as sequences of intersecting rectangles, yielding a sequential MPC framework with recursive feasibility guarantees for the LIP-based planning layer. The planner autonomously adapts to constrained scenarios, switching to in-place walking when obstructions---such as doors assumed to be open during planning but unexpectedly found to be closed during execution---block forward motion. {"arxiv_id":"2611.13379","authors":["Shiki Iwase"],"categories":["cs.RO"],"claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.13379"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"arxiv_first_submission","published_at":"2026-11-09T23:56:03Z","rule_score":70,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"Design-stage disassemblability assessment requires knowledge of product structure and the operations available in each assembly state, but CAD assemblies do not directly specify state-dependent disassembly operations. This paper proposes a fastener-centric virtual-disassembly framework that acquires such knowledge from CAD-derived virtual assemblies. Fasteners jointly releasing the same constraint are grouped into operation-level sets, avoiding enumeration of arbitrary individual-fastener orders. Their removability is evaluated through state-dependent visibility and tool-access checks and torque-driven virtual-removal trials. After fastener removal, graph-based reasoning identifies candidate moving units, whose separation is evaluated by initial-motion screening, path generation, and physics-based validation. The acquired operations, states, dependencies, validated paths, and simulation-derived attributes are organized into a Transformed AND/OR Graph for subsequent planning and design evaluation. Exhaustive verification with a controlled toy assembly found no branching violations for introduced tool-accessibility and precedence conditions. Evaluation with a 54-component OpenManipulator Chain gripper demonstrated state-dependent fastener-removal and part- or subassembly-separation operations. Visibility and tool-accessibility evaluations pruned 51.4% of fastener-set candidate evaluations, while removal of obstructing components enabled previously inaccessible fastener operations. {"arxiv_id":"2611.13382","authors":["Haejoon Lee","Thomas Marshall Vielmetti","Xinyi Wang","Dimitra Panagou"],"categories":["cs.RO","cs.LG","math.OC"],"claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.13382"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":["reinforcement_learning"],"publication_date_basis":"arxiv_first_submission","published_at":"2026-11-09T23:59:47Z","rule_score":60,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"Decision making in multi-agent and multi-robot systems often involves discrete decision variables, leading to NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems that must be solved within seconds for near real-time implementation. Abstract: Creative tool use is a fundamental human capability and an important step toward general-purpose embodied intelligence. It requires agents to reason about object affordances, physical constraints, and manipulation strategies, especially when standard tools are unavailable. However, progress in this area is limited by the lack of real-world datasets that capture human tool-use behavior with sufficient scale, fidelity, and diversity. Existing benchmarks are often simulation-based, focus on simplified interactions, or lack detailed observations and annotations.
  We introduce ToolDex, a large-scale egocentric-exocentric (ego-exo) human demonstration dataset for creative physical tool use. ToolDex captures scenarios in which humans select, adapt, and repurpose available objects as tools. Using synchronized egocentric cameras and eight exocentric cameras, the dataset provides high-fidelity multi-view observations and rich annotations for hands, tools, target objects, and their deformable interactions. Beyond data collection, we establish a benchmark suite characterizing three core capabilities: physical tool-use reasoning, sparse-view 3D and 4D reconstruction, and robot policy learning. ToolDex provides a foundation for studying human tool-use behavior and developing embodied agents that can adaptively use tools in complex real-world environments.
  Dataset visualizations and benchmarking results are available at https://tooluse-dataset.github.io/.","title":"ToolDex: An Ego-Exo Human Demonstration Dataset for Creative Physical Tool Use","title_en":"ToolDex: An Ego-Exo Human Demonstration Dataset for Creative Physical Tool Use","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.09036","version":null,"version_updated_at":null}

{"arxiv_id":"2611.12177","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Tue, 10 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.12177"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":60,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2611.12177v1 Announce Type: new \nAbstract: Early successes on agentic robotics point to a potential paradigm shift toward using coding agents to control robots. Existing robotics benchmarks are built around visuomotor policy learning, leaving it open whether coding agents can reliably control diverse robots under physical-world constraints. We therefore introduce the Embodied First Exam, a unified, comprehensive, and agent-native evaluation framework where coding agents can choose their own control approach: direct control, code to control, or train a policy to control. We hope it serves as a first exam for coding agents before they enter the physical world, with 1,156 tasks in 35 suites on 47 robots, including 9 new suites that go beyond pick-and-place to spatial puzzles, dexterous manipulation, multi-robot interaction, dynamic whole-body control, and sim-to-sim engineering. Each task can be run in up to three evaluation settings. The Standard Setting mimics the real world: the agent receives only sensor observations and, by default, cannot reset the environment. Its Realtime variant keeps the environment running while the agent reasons. The Privileged Setting gives the agent access to the full simulator state and unlimited resets, allowing it to search for an oracle solution for training purposes. Success rates in this setting serve as an approximate upper bound. On the 456 core tasks, the strongest of eight agents, GPT-6 Astra in Codex, achieves a success rate of 34% in the Standard Setting, leaving much room for improvement. To see where agents fail, we label the stage at which failed attempts go wrong and compare failures across agents, settings, and stage categories.","title":"Embodied First Exam","title_en":"Embodied First Exam","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12177","version":null,"version_updated_at":null}

{"arxiv_id":"2611.08352","authors":["Thanapong Intharah","Zhichao Gao","Yiliang Liu","Hao Dong"],"categories":["cs.CV","cs.LG","cs.RO"],"claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.08352"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"arxiv_first_submission","published_at":"2026-11-05T17:34:53Z","rule_score":70,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"Background and Objective: Our main goal is ultrasound guidance: moving a probe until its image matches a target view. Published methods for each part of a guide are evaluated in separate simulators. We asked whether these methods, combined into one guide, are good enough.
  Methods: We built USB Gym, a testbed whose standard engine simulates ultrasound from public patient CT, with a network drawing organ textures from CT labels. Its guide has three replaceable parts (slots), an organ segmenter, a controller and a reward, which received 20 published methods, each run on the same 60 episodes of six held-out patients. In each slot, a published method replaced ours only if detectably better on these patients. The better of this combination and our original guide on 20 new CTs is the benchmark baseline. A pose oracle, reading the exact probe pose available only in simulation, set the reference. The results below are exploratory.
  Results: On these CTs, the probe started on average 16.0 mm from the target view; the pose oracle brought it to 1.5 mm. Of the results known when the combination was fixed, only an image-similarity reward (SSIM) was slightly but detectably better, so the combination was our guide with that reward. This combination was the benchmark baseline, ending at 13.7 mm (16% of the oracle's progress).
  Conclusions: Combining untuned published methods with ours did not guide the probe near the target view; the task remains under-explored. The testbed accepts new methods; no guide was tested on hardware.","title":"USB Gym: A Gymnasium Testbed for Closed-Loop Ultrasound View Matching","title_en":"USB Gym: A Gymnasium Testbed for Closed-Loop Ultrasound View Matching","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.08352v1","version":"v1","version_updated_at":"2026-11-05T17:34:53Z"}

{"arxiv_id":"2611.12351","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Tue, 10 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.12351"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":60,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2611.12351v1 Announce Type: new \nAbstract: Achieving generalizable and well-aligned multimodal representations remains a core challenge in robot learning. While recent approaches have attempted to align modalities by modeling conditional or higher-order statistical dependencies, they do not explicitly consider the structural coherence across modalities. In this work, we propose a novel multimodal alignment method that augments existing contrastive losses with a geometry-aware Gromov--Wasserstein (GW) distance-based regularization. To this end, we encode intra-modal geometry for each modality and reduce cross-modal structural discrepancies through a dynamically learned GW barycenter, thereby encouraging structural consistency in addition to instance-level contrastive alignment. We apply this optimal-transport-based alignment strategy to robot perception tasks involving underexplored modalities such as force and tactile signals, where modality data often exhibit varying sample densities. Extensive experiments on five robotic benchmarks show that our method improves structural alignment and downstream performance over state-of-the-art multimodal contrastive baselines across a wide range of downstream tasks, including robot and environment state prediction. Moreover, our GW-based regularization can be seamlessly integrated into most InfoNCE-like objectives.","title":"UniOMA: Unified Optimal-Transport Multi-Modal Structural Alignment for Robot Perception","title_en":"UniOMA: Unified Optimal-Transport Multi-Modal Structural Alignment for Robot Perception","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12351","version":null,"version_updated_at":null}

{"arxiv_id":"2611.13344","authors":["Shaohong Zhong","Marco Pontin","Perla Maiolino"],"categories":["cs.RO"],"claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.13344"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"arxiv_first_submission","published_at":"2026-11-09T23:13:59Z","rule_score":90,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"Task-driven design of soft robots requires the consideration of factors such as geometry, morphology, material properties, and actuation, resulting in a large and complex design space that is challenging to explore. Computational optimisation methods leverage signals from simulation to iteratively improve designs to achieve task objectives. However, these methods typically demand high computational load for both optimisation and simulation. We present PneuGen, an agentic co-design framework for soft robots that leverages Large Language Model (LLM) agents to search over the soft robot design space efficiently. A designer agent proposes design programs from a parametric component library, and a separate critic agent analyses simulation diagnostics and recommends targeted revisions. Fitted module response models provide reusable physical priors relating geometry and pressure to deformation. Design programs are automatically validated and converted into finite-element simulations, enabling iterative evaluation. Across grasping tasks on primitive shapes and challenging objects, as well as shape-matching tasks that require multi-directional planar and 3D deformation, the proposed framework significantly outperforms prior computational optimisation baselines. Ablation experiments also highlight the utility of the critic agent and the module response model in facilitating efficient design. We additionally demonstrate the agent-generated soft robot designs in real-world shape-matching and grasping tasks.","title":"PneuGen: Task-Driven Agentic Co-Design of Soft Pneumatic Robots","title_en":"PneuGen: Task-Driven Agentic Co-Design of Soft Pneumatic Robots","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.13344v1","version":"v1","version_updated_at":"2026-11-09T23:13:59Z"}

{"arxiv_id":"2611.08097","authors":["Youhao Lyu","Chenghao Sun","Zhenxuan Ding","Shuting Zhang","Ziyang Dong","Wenhao Cui"],"categories":["cs.RO"],"claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.08097"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"arxiv_first_submission","published_at":"2026-11-05T14:40:52Z","rule_score":80,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"For perceptive humanoid locomotion, the relevance of terrain geometry depends on the robot's body state and how both evolve under its actions. Existing work has advanced terrain-aware sensory fusion and cross-modal prediction, improving how visual and proprioceptive information is combined and related. However, feature aggregation alone does not specify which cross-modal relationships should be learned, while prediction between simultaneous observations does not explicitly constrain their action-dependent evolution. We present Spatiotemporal Training with Explicit Prediction (STEP), a one-stage framework that jointly supervises cross-modal relationships and action-dependent state evolution within a shared control representation. Multiple learned queries aggregate depth and proprioceptive tokens into a compact policy state. Bidirectional masked prediction uses each visible modality to predict latent features of the omitted modality, explicitly supervising terrain-body relationships. An action-conditioned predictor maps the current policy state and executed action to the next fused state, with an exponential-moving-average target defined directly in the policy representation space. Simulation comparisons show overall improvements in terrain traversal over evaluated fusion alternatives and ablations, while depth-dropout and delay experiments demonstrate the benefits of both predictive objectives under degraded visual input. Deployed on a 23-DoF Noetix E1 humanoid with onboard sensing, STEP succeeds in 98 of 100 hardware trials across stairs, a 40\\,cm platform, a 70\\,cm gap, stepping stones, and backward stair traversal without rearward terrain visibility.","title":"STEP: Spatiotemporal Training with Explicit Prediction for Perceptive Humanoid Locomotion","title_en":"STEP: Spatiotemporal Training with Explicit Prediction for Perceptive Humanoid Locomotion","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.08097v1","version":"v1","version_updated_at":"2026-11-05T14:40:52Z"}

Yip","Yuke Zhu","Thomas Kollar","Sergey Levine","Chelsea Finn"],"categories":["cs.RO"],"claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2403.12945"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"arxiv_first_submission","published_at":"2024-03-19T17:48:38Z","rule_score":90,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"The creation of large, diverse, high-quality robot manipulation datasets is an important stepping stone on the path toward more capable and robust robotic manipulation policies. However, creating such datasets is challenging: collecting robot manipulation data in diverse environments poses logistical and safety challenges and requires substantial investments in hardware and human labour. As a result, even the most general robot manipulation policies today are mostly trained on data collected in a small number of environments with limited scene and task diversity. In this work, we introduce DROID (Distributed Robot Interaction Dataset), a diverse robot manipulation dataset with 76k demonstration trajectories or 350 hours of interaction data, collected across 564 scenes and 84 tasks by 50 data collectors in North America, Asia, and Europe over the course of 12 months. We demonstrate that training with DROID leads to policies with higher performance and improved generalization ability. {"arxiv_id":"2611.10822","authors":["Rohit Kumar Salla","Simon Stepputtis"],"categories":["cs.LG","cs.RO"],"claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.10822"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":["reinforcement_learning"],"publication_date_basis":"arxiv_first_submission","published_at":"2026-11-07T16:00:03Z","rule_score":70,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"Iterative neural policies usually spend the same computation on every decision, although the benefit of additional processing varies across states. We introduce Adaptive Internal Computation (AIC), an iterative policy that learns when to stop refining its latent representation and act. In AIC, we train action selection and stopping jointly, an expected-depth penalty values computation and intermediate value predictions provide auxiliary supervision. We show that when only some states benefit from further refinement, an ideal state-dependent allocator outperforms every state-independent stopping schedule at the same expected depth. With at most eight refinement steps per decision, AIC executes 3.3 steps on average across twelve benchmark tasks and lowers per-decision latency by 31--44% relative to a fixed eight-step policy on four control and robotics tasks. Its mean reward exceeds the best fixed-depth policy on seven tasks and trails it on four. {"arxiv_id":"2611.10994","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Tue, 10 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.10994"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":80,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2611.10994v1 Announce Type: new \nAbstract: Humanoid robots must coordinate locomotion and manipulation to navigate complex environments and perform everyday tasks. Learning such behaviours from human demonstrations requires accurate whole-body motion paired with egocentric vision, particularly for lower-body movements and foot placements that are frequently invisible from a first-person perspective. However, existing egocentric datasets often lack high-fidelity optical motion capture or systematic coverage of diverse loco-manipulation behaviours. To address this gap, we introduce RoboMoCap, a large-scale multimodal dataset combining egocentric vision with marker-based optical motion capture, specifically designed for locomotion-centric humanoid learning. RoboMoCap comprises over 200 hours of recordings from 14 participants, featuring six head-mounted cameras, wrist-mounted visual and inertial sensing, and optical full-body motion capture at 120 Hz. The dataset systematically covers diverse locomotion primitives, dynamic whole-body movements, and loco-manipulation tasks, including variable-speed walking, turning, constrained navigation, terrain traversal, object transportation, and manipulation during locomotion. It provides temporally aligned multimodal observations and metric whole-body motion representations, enabling the study of human movement beyond directly observable body regions. We systematically evaluate existing methods on three benchmark tasks: egocentric full-body motion reconstruction, foot contact and placement estimation, and human-to-humanoid motion retargeting. By pairing egocentric vision with high-fidelity human motion across diverse locomotion and interaction scenarios, RoboMoCap provides a foundation for egocentric motion understanding and humanoid learning from human demonstrations.","title":"RoboMoCap: A Large-Scale Whole-Body Motion Capture Dataset with Egocentric Vision for Robot Learning","title_en":"RoboMoCap: A Large-Scale Whole-Body Motion Capture Dataset with Egocentric Vision for Robot Learning","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.10994","version":null,"version_updated_at":null}

Previously, the MultiMediate challenge has focused on estimating momentary continuous engagement values in adult conversation across cultures, achieving high levels of generalisability across domains. However, engagement can be measured in different metrics and manifest differently between children and adults. MultiMediate'26 therefore expands the evaluated domain set to include the PInSoRo dataset of Child-Child and Child-Robot play sessions in English. These sessions were annotated categorically with task and social engagement, diversifying engagement types, age ranges and interaction types. Here, we extend the methodology to learn aSSM-reduced models from data collected from hardware soft robotic platforms. Specifically, we learn a five dimensional (5D) aSSM-reduced nonlinear ordinary differential equation (ODE) that accurately models the dynamics of a soft-helicoid trunk robot. We then use this ODE in a model predictive control scheme to demonstrate real-time precision control across various challenging closed-loop trajectory-tracking tasks, ranging from 2D to 3D trajectories with static and dynamic constraints. We find that our methodology enhances accuracy and precision across all control tasks compared to available data-driven linear methods and model-free reinforcement learning. While we focus here on a soft-helicoid trunk robot, our methodology relies solely on hardware data and is therefore applicable to a broader class of soft robotic systems.","title":"Data-Driven Precision Control of Soft Helicoid Robots","title_en":"Data-Driven Precision Control of Soft Helicoid Robots","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.11709","version":null,"version_updated_at":null}

{"arxiv_id":"2610.07910","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Mon, 09 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2610.07910"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":["reinforcement_learning"],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":60,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2610.07910v3 Announce Type: replace-cross \nAbstract: Deep Reinforcement Learning policies can produce nonsmooth action oscillations that hinder deployment on physical robots. Existing architectural and penalty-based approaches seek spatial smoothness by directly reducing sensitivity to changes in state inputs, but their broad constraints can degrade task performance as stronger smoothing is pursued. Temporal regularization instead constrains action differences along observed transitions, but has been considered unable to provide the spatial smoothness needed under observation noise. We revisit this assumption by proving that the temporal penalty bounds the expected action differences between current states sharing a next state, revealing a spatial effect that empirically extends to spatial smoothness. Building on this finding, we propose Conditioning for Action using only Temporal Smoothness (CATS), which combines a temporal penalty with linear ramp-up. We highlight temporal regularization's ability to provide spatial smoothness while better preserving task performance than explicit spatial regularization. This report investigates BCVS (budget-aware correspondence-driven view sampling), a pose-free view selection algorithm that offers 22+ FPS on a CPU, enabling online filtering for efficient 3D perception by mobile robots. Unlike existing approaches that rely on full structure-from-motion (SfM) pipelines or camera pose estimation, BCVS employs a purely correspondence-based scoring strategy that prioritizes view novelty while maintaining sufficient overlap for geometric stability. Given a user-specified budget, BCVS iteratively selects the most distinct frames and suppresses near-duplicates, producing compact subsets that preserve connectivity and minimize reconstruction loss. Extensive experiments on benchmark show that BCVS outperforms CPU-friendly baselines at tight budgets and remains competitive as budgets scale. Field trials with large aerial and marine robotics data further validate its practicality and scalability: BCVS reduces redundancy up to 16% while sustaining robust SfM registration and high-quality 3D reconstructions.","title":"Budget-aware Correspondence-driven View Selection for Real-time 3D Perception of Mobile Robots","title_en":"Budget-aware Correspondence-driven View Selection for Real-time 3D Perception of Mobile Robots","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.11809","version":null,"version_updated_at":null}

{"arxiv_id":"2611.09905","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Tue, 10 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.09905"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":50,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2611.09905v1 Announce Type: cross \nAbstract: As social robots become increasingly present in everyday environments, establishing rapport with users is critical for enabling sustained and meaningful human-robot interaction. In human-human communication, self-disclosure is a well-established mechanism for building rapport; however, its role and impact in human-robot interaction (HRI) are not yet well understood. Although recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have improved the linguistic competence of conversational robots, such systems are typically deployed as reactive information providers, offering limited social reciprocity and relational depth. In this article, we investigate the role of robot self-disclosure in fostering rapport during face-to-face human-robot interaction. We propose a dialogue system, called RADIA that leverages retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to enable a robot to retrieve and reference simulated autobiographical memories, allowing first-person self-disclosure to be incorporated naturally into ongoing conversations. We evaluate the proposed approach through an in-person user study, comparing interactions with a self-disclosing robot against a baseline non-self-disclosing robot. Our results show that robot self-disclosure significantly influences conversational dynamics and enhances users' perceived rapport with the robot, suggesting that self-disclosure is a valuable social behavior for long-term and socially engaging human-robot interaction.","title":"Building Rapport with Self-Disclosure in Human-Robot Interaction","title_en":"Building Rapport with Self-Disclosure in Human-Robot Interaction","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.09905","version":null,"version_updated_at":null}

{"arxiv_id":"2606.22682","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Tue, 10 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2606.22682"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":60,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2606.22682v2 Announce Type: replace \nAbstract: The imperative to develop more sustainable agriculture demands a transition from isolated automation toward the deployment of multi-robot systems (MRS) in agrifood environments. However, Mediterranean greenhouse settings-characterized by narrow corridors, dense biomass, and structural metallic interference-pose significant challenges for robust and scalable communication between agents. Traditional robotic frameworks, such as ROS 2, frequently encounter node discovery issues and latency spikes due to dynamic obstacles, dense foliage, and other characteristic greenhouse elements, creating a critical bottleneck for real-time coordination. This paper proposes an innovative cloud-based hybrid architecture that establishes a two-way communication bridge between ROS 2, acting as an edge computing platform, and iVeg as a Decision Support System (DSS), using MQTT and the European FIWARE platform. The proposed framework enables seamless interoperability between fleets of multiple robots in environments with communication constraints, facilitating the synchronised exchange of high-level telemetry, point cloud data and farmer identification for collaboration, amongst other critical data. The architecture was validated in a high-fidelity simulation environment and subsequently tested in a real-world greenhouse scenario, demonstrating its ability to maintain persistent connectivity and data integrity under adverse network conditions. The results indicate that the integration of MQTT effectively eliminates information silos, providing a scalable and decentralised solution for managing complex robotic missions, which are executed locally via Edge Computing. This work sets a new methodological precedent for the concept of Greenhouse Models as a Service (GMaaS), bridging the gap between low-level robotic control and high-level, cloud-based IoT decision-making.","title":"Integrated hybrid edge-cloud architecture for multi-robot and human-robot collaboration using ROS 2-MQTT-FIWARE in Mediterranean Greenhouses","title_en":"Integrated hybrid edge-cloud architecture for multi-robot and human-robot collaboration using ROS 2-MQTT-FIWARE in Mediterranean Greenhouses","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.22682","version":null,"version_updated_at":null}

{"arxiv_id":"2611.08295","authors":["Gabriel Parra","Kimia Khoshnami","Daniel S. Brown","Laura A. Hallock"],"categories":["cs.RO","cs.HC","cs.LG"],"claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.08295"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"arxiv_first_submission","published_at":"2026-11-05T16:55:55Z","rule_score":80,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"Robot-mediated rehabilitation has the potential to deliver high-intensity, individualized therapy, but existing systems (which have not consistently improved outcomes) typically prescribe kinematic trajectories rather than explicitly targeting the neuromotor activations thought to support recovery. To address this gap, and ultimately enable activation-optimizing rehabilitation robot behavior, we present a personalizable transformer-based model mapping individuals' muscle activations (as measured via surface electromyography) to prescribed contact force trajectories when interacting with an end-effector rehabilitation robot. The model uses a transformer encoder-decoder leveraging rotary positional embeddings (RoPE) to generate a latent representation of trajectory-relevant and user-specific neuromotor factors, and augments trajectory prediction with flow matching to produce a distribution over plausible prescriptions biased toward the training distribution. Using data from 16 healthy participants completing 15 isometric trajectory tracking tasks, we evaluate generalization across held-out tasks and users, as well as the feasibility of user-specific fine-tuning within a therapy-session timescale. The model achieves mean trajectory prediction errors of  < 8% on held out tasks and users, with effectively instantaneous deterministic inference and sub-second sampling of trajectory distributions. An initial test using the model during live rehabilitation tasks demonstrates that, on average, participants reach the target neuromotor activations with just 15% error accumulated throughout the task. These results provide a proof of concept for data-driven, activation-targeted trajectory prescription in robot-mediated rehabilitation and establish a foundation for future validation in clinical populations. Data and code have been open-sourced as part of the OpenRobotRehab project on SimTK.","title":"Transformer-Based Trajectory Prescription for sEMG-Optimizing Robot-Mediated Rehabilitation","title_en":"Transformer-Based Trajectory Prescription for sEMG-Optimizing Robot-Mediated Rehabilitation","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.08295v1","version":"v1","version_updated_at":"2026-11-05T16:55:55Z"}

{"arxiv_id":"2611.11978","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Tue, 10 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.11978"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":80,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2611.11978v1 Announce Type: new \nAbstract: Zero-shot object-goal navigation requires autonomous agents to explore unseen environments and locate target objects without task-specific training, posing challenges in perceptual reliability under observation uncertainty and physically grounded goal termination. Although foundation-model-based approaches improve generalization, they remain vulnerable to unreliable long-range perception, hallucination-induced directional bias, and semantically plausible but geometrically incorrect stopping decisions. To address these limitations, we propose CSG-Nav, a zero-shot navigation framework centered on confidence-aware multimodal information fusion. CSG-Nav integrates three complementary fusion mechanisms. First, semantic-source fusion integrates open-vocabulary detection results, detection confidence, scene observations, and relational reasoning to produce more reliable direction-level semantic scores and suppress hallucination-induced directional bias. Second, spatial-confidence fusion weights multi-view semantic evidence using a Gaussian decay function, suppressing unreliable distant observations while accumulating spatially consistent exploration preferences. Third, semantic-geometric decision fusion combines semantic target detection with depth-based 3D localization to support physically grounded stopping decisions. Experiments on HM3Dv1, HM3Dv2, and MP3D demonstrate competitive zero-shot performance, achieving success rates of 58.9%, 71.6%, and 44.3%. Fusion-level ablations and real-world deployments in indoor and outdoor environments further verify the effectiveness and practicality of CSG-Nav for robust navigation under uncertain perception. Code is available at https://xr-ui.github.io/CSGNav.github.io/","title":"CSG-Nav: Confidence-Aware Semantic-Geometric Fusion for Robust Exploration and Accurate Zero-Shot Object-Goal Navigation","title_en":"CSG-Nav: Confidence-Aware Semantic-Geometric Fusion for Robust Exploration and Accurate Zero-Shot Object-Goal Navigation","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.11978","version":null,"version_updated_at":null}

{"arxiv_id":"2610.08220","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Mon, 09 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2610.08220"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":["vla"],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":80,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2610.08220v2 Announce Type: replace \nAbstract: Portable mobile-manipulation demonstrations can help alleviate data scarcity for embodied intelligence, but obtaining reliable, low-cost, and robot-free motion supervision from RGB observations remains challenging. Existing approaches often rely on teleoperation or specialized devices equipped with additional sensing hardware, while directly using estimated visual odometry (VO) trajectories can introduce inconsistencies due to accumulated drift and imperfect motion supervision. We present the Visual-Odometry-Conditioned Mobile Manipulation Interface (VOMMI), a portable demonstration collection and learning framework that connects portable RGB demonstrations to vision-language-action (VLA) post-training through offline trajectory reconstruction and online visual-motion conditioning. VOMMI synchronizes body and hand views to capture navigation context and local object interactions without requiring human-robot kinematic correspondence calibration. R2-VO refines offline demonstration trajectories using sparse geometric anchors and produces causal local-motion tokens over multiple prediction horizons for online policy conditioning. An action-group residual adapter incorporates these tokens only into the base branch. Experiments use a 500-trajectory portable for each task, with 75 trajectories held out for RGB-VO evaluation, and 200 robot demonstrations as references. Our policy, post-trained only on portable demonstrations, achieves 18.2% lower base-velocity error than a policy trained with robot-collected demonstrations, while maintaining comparable end-effector translation accuracy. Offline reconstruction reduces absolute trajectory errors for the body and hand streams by 24.6% on average relative to the best evaluated baseline for each stream. The complete system improves the mean success rate by 8.3 percentage points over OpenPI 0.5 across three real-robot tasks.","title":"VOMMI: Collecting and Leveraging Portable Demonstrations for Mobile Manipulation","title_en":"VOMMI: Collecting and Leveraging Portable Demonstrations for Mobile Manipulation","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.08220","version":null,"version_updated_at":null}

{"arxiv_id":"2611.09794","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Mon, 09 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.09794"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":70,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2611.09794v1 Announce Type: new \nAbstract: When should a robot look at the cup, and when at the portafilter? Spatial-reasoning benchmarks evaluate whether a model can describe a scene, but manipulation needs something more specific: the ability to acquire the particular evidence that makes the current command executable. A view that is informative for one task can be useless for another, even at the same workstation. We introduce Seeing What Matters, a benchmark for task-conditioned actionable spatial belief in simulated tabletop manipulation. Across three domains--coffee workstation, drawer/cabinet, and microwave/appliance--the benchmark provides 860 frozen evaluation cases; expanding across methods, budgets, and inference repeats yields more than 115,000 evaluator episodes under two protocols: closed-loop actionability and same-object functional out-of-distribution generalization. Each case pairs a set of candidate RGB views with a manipulation command, shared scripted skills, and hidden postconditions, so the benchmark directly measures whether a view-selection policy acquires the observations its command actually needs. We also provide a diagnostic reference pipeline that maintains a spatial-functional belief state and ranks views by missing evidence. At primary budget settings, this pipeline reaches 98.8% closed-loop and 98.9% functional-OOD success; ablating the functional or command-binding components collapses performance to near zero. Seven vision-language models, evaluated on the same cases, reach only 26-43%. Replacing the reference pipeline's coverage metadata with frozen RGB-derived scores preserves 98.5%/98.9% success; shuffling the visual scores collapses it to 15%/11%, confirming that the result depends on image content. These gaps suggest that spatial belief for manipulation should be evaluated not by scene-level completeness, but by whether it acquires the evidence the current command requires.","title":"Seeing What Matters: Benchmarking Task-Conditioned Actionable Spatial Belief for Manipulation","title_en":"Seeing What Matters: Benchmarking Task-Conditioned Actionable Spatial Belief for Manipulation","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.09794","version":null,"version_updated_at":null}

We present SENTINEL, a training - free, label - free reliability estimation framework that gives range - only LiDAR an effective diagnostic signal. SENTINEL combines geometry-based scan statistics with cross - modal depth consistency between LiDAR and an RGB - D camera to compute a per - scan reliability score between 0 and 1. When the score falls below a threshold, corrupted scans are rejected and the robot falls back to calibrated wheel odometry, preventing silent SLAM corruption. We evaluate SENTINEL on a GEFIER R1 four - wheel skid-steer robot equipped with an RPLidar A2M12 and an Intel RealSense D435i in a 185 cm by 245 cm arena containing controlled transparent and reflective failure elements on a central obstacle. Spatial reliability maps across five surface conditions, including glass, mirror, shiny paper, and a mixed mirror and shiny-paper condition, show clear separation between clean and failure cases, allowing affected regions to be identified as reject or noise. Because these failure modes are absent in simulation, validation is performed entirely on real hardware.","title":"Teaching Robots to Say 'I Don't Know' : SENTINEL for Uncertainty-Aware SLAM","title_en":"Teaching Robots to Say 'I Don't Know' : SENTINEL for Uncertainty-Aware SLAM","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.04853","version":null,"version_updated_at":null}

The adapter estimates measurement dropout over each predicted surface, allowing the selection method to favor views likely to fill gaps in the measured reconstruction. The adapted method recovers a surface region that the nominal method repeatedly targets but fails to measure. {"arxiv_id":"2611.11856","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Tue, 10 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.11856"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":["vla"],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":50,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2611.11856v1 Announce Type: cross \nAbstract: Fleets of driving vision-language-action (VLA) models are developed one domain at a time: each operator finetunes a shared base model on private data, producing specialized experts that are costly to consolidate into a single model. Weight merging loses accuracy as heterogeneous domains accumulate, and dense mixture-of-experts routing is prohibitively expensive to combine them. We present DeltaForge, to our knowledge the first post-hoc mixture-of-experts VLA for driving, which consolidates N independently finetuned per-domain models into a single multi-domain model from their weights and a small proxy set alone. When different operators finetune the same base model, their weight updates end up sharing a lot of structure. We exploit this by decomposing all the updates together using singular value decomposition (SVD), splitting each one into a shared part (the same across all domains) and a tiny domain-specific part. The router then only needs to work with those tiny domain-specific pieces, not the full expert weights, which is what keeps the approach efficient. Then two cooperating clip-level blind routers, one over the VLM reasoning experts and one over the flow-matching dynamics experts, are trained from soft labels on the proxy dataset. Across six diverse domains spanning urban, off-road, and highway driving on cars, trucks, and all-terrain vehicles (ATVs), DeltaForge approaches the accuracy of the per-domain experts and surpasses every merging, routing, centralized, and federated baseline at close to single-model parameter and compute cost. Adding a new domain requires only projecting its weight update onto the shared basis with no end-to-end retraining needed. The resulting model also generalizes to domain combinations it was never explicitly trained on.","title":"DeltaForge: A Post-hoc Mixture-of-Experts VLA for Multi-Domain Autonomous Driving","title_en":"DeltaForge: A Post-hoc Mixture-of-Experts VLA for Multi-Domain Autonomous Driving","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.11856","version":null,"version_updated_at":null}

{"arxiv_id":"2606.04569","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Tue, 10 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2606.04569"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":["reinforcement_learning"],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":80,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2606.04569v2 Announce Type: replace \nAbstract: Underground mines present extreme conditions for autonomous robot navigation: GPS is denied, lighting is degraded, and tunnel topology is loop-rich and non-convex. Simulation benchmarks grounded in real production-mine geometry and compatible with GPU-accelerated learning pipelines do not yet exist in the open-source ecosystem. We present MineXplore, an open-source MuJoCo-based navigation benchmark derived from the Leung et al. 2017 Chilean underground copper mine dataset. The environment reconstructs a 104,423 sq.m tunnel network through an six-stage contour-to-MJCF pipeline incorporating octagonal wall cross-sections, LiDAR-sourced jagged wall geometry, three terrain friction zones, a global 5 degree incline, and periodic spot lighting. Geometric fidelity is validated at an Intersection over Union (IoU) of 0.9538 against the source survey map, and surface texture similarity scores 79.4% across six structural dimensions. {"arxiv_id":"2606.13355","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Mon, 09 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2606.13355"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":["diffusion_policy","vla"],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":50,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2606.13355v2 Announce Type: replace \nAbstract: Real-time execution, enabled by asynchronous inference that ensures both smooth action trajectories and fast reactivity, is critical for realistic deployments of large-scale Vision-Language-Action models. However, recent work on real-time execution primarily focuses on variants of diffusion policies, even though it is more critical for autoregressive policies given their slower rollout speed in synchronous inference. In contrast, we demonstrate that autoregressive policies can achieve real-time execution by adjusting the tokenization horizon and applying constrained decoding, thereby guaranteeing strict latency bounds that enable multi-trajectory decoding to maximize performance. Every predicted step must be computed on board within a tight power and thermal budget, yet the energy these steps fundamentally require, and how far real hardware sits from it, have not been characterized. {"arxiv_id":"2611.11286","authors":["Tielin Ma","Junlin Zhang","Jingcheng Fu","Chongwen Jiang","Chuan Ye"],"categories":["physics.flu-dyn","cs.CE","cs.RO"],"claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.11286"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"arxiv_first_submission","published_at":"2026-11-08T10:13:29Z","rule_score":50,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"Helically stranded cables in aerial towing systems experience oblique inflow, but are often modeled as smooth cylinders, neglecting three-dimensional cross-stream coupling and surface texture. Aerodynamic differences are governed mainly by cross-sectional symmetry and strand-scale groove depth. Force-source decomposition shows that surface pressure contributes 94.9%--98.3% of the mean normal force and dominates the mean lateral force. High-symmetry, quasi-circular envelopes maintain balanced circumferential pressure, whereas deep-grooved, low-symmetry tri-lobed geometries produce asymmetric separation and a persistent lateral pressure imbalance. In the wake, high-symmetry cables sustain spanwise-synchronized Karman shedding at moderate-to-high inclinations, concentrating fluctuation energy in a dominant low-rank mode. Deep grooves disrupt shedding coherence, deflect the recirculation zone laterally, and spread energy across broadband scales. Mean lateral force and lateral-force fluctuations are therefore decoupled: the quasi-circular $(1 \\times 19)$ cable has minimal mean lateral force but strong periodic fluctuations, while the deep-grooved $(3 \\times 7)$ cable has weak fluctuations but appreciable mean lateral force. Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), with their strong generalization, are a promising foundation for such agents. We propose GTA, a decoupled design that separates low-level spatial state estimation from high-level semantic planning. We introduce an explicit metric world representation that combines accumulated geometry with navigation history and exposes this information to the MLLM through a multimodal interface for decision-making. We further introduce counterfactual branch reasoning that checks anticipated outcomes against subsequent observations and revises navigation decisions when they disagree. The world representation grounds waypoint selection in reconstructed metric geometry. GTA achieves 48.8% Success Rate (SR) on the full R2R-CE val-unseen split and 46.2% on a 260-episode English RxR-CE val-unseen subset. We introduce an asynchronous inference and control framework that enables fast task execution while maintaining smooth and stable robot motions. By formulating the generation of continuous target positions from discontinuous model predictions as a tracking control problem, our method makes asynchronous inference practical for real robots. {"arxiv_id":"2611.09906","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Tue, 10 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.09906"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":40,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2611.09906v1 Announce Type: cross \nAbstract: Proactively initiating a conversation is a fundamental social competence and a critical capability for social robots. However, determining how and when to start a conversation in a given situation remains an open challenge, primarily due to the lack of a principled definition of conversational context. While recent large language models (LLMs) demonstrate impressive conversational fluency, they are predominantly turn-reactive and often produce generic or monotonous openers when tasked with initiating interaction, even when contextual information is available. Such limitations are particularly problematic for embodied social robots, where inappropriate or poorly timed initiations can negatively affect user engagement and rapport. In this work, we propose a schema of contextual variables that jointly characterize situations relevant for proactive conversation initiation. The schema is designed to structure perceptual, situational, and interactional cues such that they can be effectively exploited by language models. Furthermore, motivated by the absence of suitable training data, we introduce a curated dataset of contextually-aligned conversation openers (CCO) covering diverse everyday scenarios. Using this dataset, we fine-tune small language models (SLMs) to generate proactive conversation initiations. Through a comparative evaluation involving zero-shot LLMs, off-the-shelf SLMs, and our fine-tuned models, we demonstrate that explicit contextual structuring and targeted data curation substantially improve the quality and contextual appropriateness of conversation openers. Our results highlight the importance of context modeling for proactive social interaction and provide actionable building blocks for conversational robots.","title":"How to start a conversation proactively?","title_en":"How to start a conversation proactively?","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.09906","version":null,"version_updated_at":null}

{"arxiv_id":"2605.19919","claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","date_note":"RSS announcement is not the original submission date; API verification is pending.","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","feed_announced_at":"Tue, 10 Nov 2026 00:00:00 -0500","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2605.19919"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":["reinforcement_learning"],"publication_date_basis":"unknown","published_at":null,"rule_score":80,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"arXiv:2605.19919v2 Announce Type: replace \nAbstract: Pretrained imitation policies have become a strong foundation for robot manipulation, but online adaptation can further improve policy performance within their pretrained behavioral support. A central question is therefore how reinforcement learning (RL) should adapt policies after offline pretraining. Existing lightweight methods commonly apply residual corrections directly in action space. We investigate how the steering interface affects online RL. In this work, we propose Z-Perturbation Reinforcement Learning (ZPRL), an approach that steers pretrained policies through a compact bottleneck latent rather than through policy weights or output actions. Building on an offline-learned bottleneck policy interface introduced by previous work, ZPRL turns this representation into an online RL control space through reward-driven residual perturbations while freezing the pretrained policy. We instantiate ZPRL on flow-matching policies and evaluate it on eight simulation tasks and four real-world tasks. Across diverse manipulation settings, ZPRL improves sample efficiency with competitive or better final performance. In the real world, ZPRL improves the average success rate on four tasks by 33.7 percentage points over imitation base policies. Our qualitative and quantitative results also indicate that ZPRL combines task success with smooth actions without explicit temporal filtering or smoothness regularization. These results suggest that a compact, task-aligned bottleneck latent provides an effective interface for online RL adaptation. Moreover, during the flight these sensors might move because of external disturbances and cause a CoM offset.
